qs.answer: The written record settles most doubts
qs.why: Catatan di buku itu menjawab hampir semua pertanyaan soal belanja kecil, jadi nggak ada lagi bahan berdebat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Uang jajan nggak pernah disebut naik, orang tua memeriksa cuma sekali sepekan, dan amplop ketiga justru nggak boleh disentuh.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The family may spend the emergency envelope on ordinary shopping."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The family may spend the emergency envelope on ordinary shopping.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Money in the third envelope may not be touched for anything else.
qs.why: Uang di amplop ketiga nggak boleh dipakai untuk hal lain, jadi klaim boleh dipakai belanja biasa bertentangan.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” melanggar aturan yang tertulis; “Not stated” gugur karena larangannya disebut langsung.

author: family life columnist
setting: a family home in a small town

title: Why City Air Stays Warm
text:
Anyone who walks through a big city in the afternoon knows the feeling. The pavement burns, and the air stays warm long after sunset. Scientists call this the urban heat island. Roads, roofs and walls take in sunlight all day and hold it. At night the stored heat leaves the concrete slowly, so the city cools far later than the fields around it.

Green space changes the picture. A row of trees can drop the temperature under it by a few degrees, because leaves give shade and release water vapour. Light-coloured roofs help too, since pale paint sends sunlight back to the sky. In Bandung, one school painted its roof white and watched the classrooms for a month. The rooms stayed cooler in the afternoon, and the fans were switched on less often.

Small choices matter here. Every new tree, garden and pale wall takes a little heat out of the street, and the whole neighbourhood shares the benefit.
qs: Overall, what point does this text make about heat in a city?
Roads take in sunlight, so fans are the only answer.
Trees give shade, and pale walls make streets warmer.
Cities hold heat, but plants and pale surfaces cool them.
A school painted its roof, but the rooms stayed as hot.

qs.evidence: Every new tree, garden and pale wall takes a little heat out of the street, and the whole neighbourhood shares the benefit.
qs.answer: Cities hold heat, but plants and pale surfaces cool them.
qs.why: Kalimat penutup nyimpulin dua hal: kota nyimpen panas dan tanaman plus warna pucat nurunin panas itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jalan memang nyimpen panas, tapi teks nggak pernah bilang kipas satu-satunya jalan keluar. Dinding pucat justru nurunin panas, bukan naikin. Sekolah di Bandung disebut sebagai contoh yang berhasil, jadi “ruangnya tetap panas” berlawanan.

qs: Overall, why does a city cool down later than the land around it?
Because the fields around it hold much more water.
Because hard surfaces let go of the trapped warmth slowly.
Because tall buildings block the wind along the streets.
Because the pavement takes in sunlight after sunset.

qs.evidence: At night the stored heat leaves the concrete slowly, so the city cools far later than the fields around it.
qs.answer: Because hard surfaces let go of the trapped warmth slowly.
qs.why: “Hard surfaces” itu jalan dan beton; teks bilang panasnya keluar pelan-pelan dari beton.
qs.whyOthersFail: Air di ladang sekitar nggak pernah dibahas teks. Angin yang ketahan gedung tinggi juga nggak disebut sama sekali. Trotoar memang nyerap sinar, tapi siang hari, bukan sesudah matahari terbenam.

qs: In paragraph 1, what does "take in" mean?
hold on to the day's heat
throw the sunlight back at the sky
let warmth escape into the air
soak up energy from the sun

qs.evidence: Roads, roofs and walls take in sunlight all day and hold it.
qs.answer: soak up energy from the sun
qs.why: Di sini “take in” dipasangin sama “hold it”, jadi maksudnya nyerap, bukan nolak.
qs.whyOthersFail: “Menahan panas” itu bagian “hold it”, kerja sesudah menyerap, bukan arti “take in”. Memantulkan cahaya ke langit justru kerja cat pucat. Melepas panas ke udara itu tahap malam di teks.

qs: What is likely to happen to a street once a row of young trees grows there?
The air under the trees will become a few degrees cooler.
The pavement will store more heat during the day.
The street will cool down later than the fields nearby.
The fans in the nearby rooms will run for longer.

qs.evidence: A row of trees can drop the temperature under it by a few degrees, because leaves give shade and release water vapour.
qs.answer: The air under the trees will become a few degrees cooler.
qs.why: Sebaris pohon bisa menurunkan suhu di bawahnya beberapa derajat karena daun memberi naungan dan melepas uap air.
qs.whyOthersFail: Permukaan keras menyimpan panas justru karena bahannya, bukan karena ada pohon. Kota memang mendingin lebih lambat daripada ladang, tapi itu keadaan tanpa naungan. Contoh di Bandung menunjukkan kipas malah lebih jarang dinyalakan saat ruangan lebih sejuk.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Trees lower the temperature partly by giving off water vapour."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Trees lower the temperature partly by giving off water vapour.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: A row of trees can drop the temperature under it by a few degrees, because leaves give shade and release water vapour.
qs.why: Teks nulis daun ngasih naungan dan “release water vapour”; klaimnya cuma ganti kata jadi “giving off”.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” nggak bisa karena nggak ada proposisi yang dibalik; “Not stated” nggak bisa karena sebabnya ditulis di kalimat itu.

author: Environment desk
setting: a warm Indonesian city

title: Choir Takes Silver at the District Festival
text:
The school choir came home from the district festival on Saturday with a silver medal. Forty singers from Years 10 and 11 travelled to the city hall by bus. They performed two pieces: a traditional song from Flores and a gentle song in English.

The judges praised the group for clear words. However, they marked it down on balance. The report sheet records that the male voices were too soft in the second piece. Ms Ratna, who has trained the singers since March, said the result was fair. "We practised the English song for only three weeks," she remarked. "Next time we shall begin earlier."

Practice continues on Wednesday afternoon in the music room. The group requires eight more voices, and any pupil may join after an informal listening test. Ms Ratna will arrange the tests during the first week of the new term. The list of times is already on the board outside the staff room.
qs: Overall, what does this report tell readers about the school choir?
How the judges scored balance, and why clear words matter.
What the singers achieved and what they plan next.
How forty singers travelled, and where they will sing again.
When the tests happen, and who may join the choir.

qs.evidence: The school choir came home from the district festival on Saturday with a silver medal.
qs.answer: What the singers achieved and what they plan next.
qs.why: Laporannya dua bagian: hasil lomba plus rencana latihan dan tes anggota baru.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penilaian juri dan pentingnya artikulasi cuma satu bagian laporan. Perjalanan empat puluh penyanyi juga latar, dan tempat tampil berikutnya nggak ditulis. Jadwal tes memang ada, tapi itu langkah lanjutan, bukan isi pokoknya.

qs: What weakness did the judges find?
The men in the group sang too quietly in one piece.
The singers did not pronounce the words clearly.
The choir sang the English song faster than planned.
The group was smaller than the other choirs there.

qs.evidence: The report sheet records that the male voices were too soft in the second piece.
qs.answer: The men in the group sang too quietly in one piece.
qs.why: “Male voices were too soft” sama artinya sama cowok-cowoknya nyanyi terlalu pelan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Soal kejelasan kata, juri justru memuji, jadi itu kebalikannya. Tempo lagu Inggris dan jumlah anggota dibanding paduan suara lain nggak pernah ditulis di laporan.

qs: What must a pupil do before joining the choir?
Bring a note from a parent to Ms Ratna
Learn the song from Flores before the first practice
Sit a brief test of the ear with the teacher
Practise with the group on Wednesday afternoon first

qs.evidence: The group requires eight more voices, and any pupil may join after an informal listening test.
qs.answer: Sit a brief test of the ear with the teacher
qs.why: “Listening test” itu tes dengar singkat; teks bilang siapa pun boleh masuk sesudah tes itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Surat izin orang tua nggak disebut sebagai syarat. Lagu Flores memang dinyanyiin di festival, tapi nggak jadi syarat masuk. Latihan Rabu itu kegiatan rutin, bukan langkah sebelum diterima.

qs: Why did Ms Ratna call the silver medal fair?
Because silver is the usual result for a first year
Because the judges found fault with the clear words
Because the choir is still eight voices short
Because the group had little time on one song

qs.evidence: "We practised the English song for only three weeks," she remarked.
qs.answer: Because the group had little time on one song
qs.why: Dia langsung nyambungin hasilnya sama latihan yang cuma tiga minggu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak bilang perak itu hasil biasa buat pendatang baru. Kata-kata yang jelas justru dipuji juri. Kurang delapan suara itu urusan rekrutmen, bukan alasan nilainya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Ms Ratna has led the choir since the start of this term."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Ms Ratna has led the choir since the start of this term.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Ms Ratna, who has trained the singers since March, said the result was fair.
qs.why: Teks bilang dia latih paduan suara sejak Maret, jadi waktu mulainya beda dari “awal term ini”.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena titik waktunya ditukar; “Not stated” salah karena lama dia melatih memang ditulis.

author: School news team
setting: a secondary school and the district festival hall

title: Why the Group Chat Feels So Loud
text:
A class group chat can send a hundred messages before breakfast. Most of them are useful: a photo of the homework, a question about the bus, a reminder about football practice, a joke. The trouble begins when the device buzzes for every single message. Each buzz breaks your concentration, and you need about a minute to recover.

Three habits make the noise easier to live with. First, mute the chat and open it twice a day, at lunch and after dinner. Second, agree on one channel for urgent notices, so nobody has to scroll past jokes to find an exam date. Third, keep replies brief; a simple symbol is enough.

Rina, a Year 11 pupil, tried this plan for two weeks. She still examined every message, but she checked the chat only at fixed times. Her marks did not change, she says, yet her evenings felt longer and far more peaceful.
qs: Overall, what point does this text make about a busy class group chat?
Chats are useful, and a few habits keep them bearable.
Every buzz breaks focus, and marks fall as a result.
One channel carries notices, and the rest can be muted.
Rina muted her chat, and her marks rose by a grade.

qs.evidence: Three habits make the noise easier to live with.
qs.answer: Chats are useful, and a few habits keep them bearable.
qs.why: Teks ngakui chat itu berguna, terus nawarin tiga kebiasaan biar nggak berisik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak bilang nilai jatuh gara-gara notifikasi; yang disebut fokus terganggu semenit. Soal satu kanal itu usulan, bukan pokok tulisan, dan teks nggak nyuruh matiin sisanya. Nilai Rina justru nggak turun, bukan naik satu tingkat.

qs: What happens every time the phone buzzes?
The message moves to the top of the chat list.
Most pupils reply at once with a short symbol.
Your focus leaves the task for roughly a minute.
The homework photo opens on your screen.

qs.evidence: Each buzz breaks your concentration, and you need about a minute to recover.
qs.answer: Your focus leaves the task for roughly a minute.
qs.why: Sekali bunyi, fokusmu pecah dan butuh sekitar satu menit buat balik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Urutan pesan di daftar chat nggak pernah dibahas teks. Balasan pakai simbol itu saran ketiga, bukan yang terjadi tiap getaran. Foto PR cuma contoh isi chat, bukan efek bunyinya.

qs: Which habit does the article suggest first?
Agreeing on one channel for urgent notices
Silencing the chat and opening it twice daily
Keeping every reply as short as possible
Checking the chat only after dinner each day

qs.evidence: First, mute the chat and open it twice a day, at lunch and after dinner.
qs.answer: Silencing the chat and opening it twice daily
qs.why: Saran nomor satu: senyapin chatnya, terus buka dua kali sehari.
qs.whyOthersFail: Satu kanal buat kabar penting itu saran kedua dan balasan singkat saran ketiga, jadi urutannya salah. Buka cuma sesudah makan malam juga keliru: teks minta dua kali sehari.

qs: What does Rina's fortnight suggest?
Muting a chat may lift a pupil's marks a little.
Reading fewer messages tends to make pupils miss news.
A busy class chat probably suits older pupils best.
Opening a chat less often need not cost you marks.

qs.evidence: Her marks did not change, she says, yet her evenings felt longer and far more peaceful.
qs.answer: Opening a chat less often need not cost you marks.
qs.why: Nilainya tetap padahal dia buka chat cuma di jam tertentu, jadi ngurangin akses nggak otomatis bikin nilai turun.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang nilainya nggak berubah, jadi nilai naik pun nggak didukung. Rina tetap baca semua pesan, jadi soal ketinggalan kabar nggak nyambung. Umur pengguna chat nggak pernah dibahas.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Rina skipped none of the messages during her two weeks."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Rina skipped none of the messages during her two weeks.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: She still examined every message, but she checked the chat only at fixed times.
qs.why: Teks nulis dia tetap baca semua pesan, artinya nggak ada yang dilewat.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh bagian yang dibalik dan nggak ada; “Not stated” nggak pas karena kebiasaan bacanya disebut langsung.

author: Digital habits column
setting: phones and chat groups of Year 11 pupils

title: Email: About Your Sleep Diary
text:
Dear Adit, thank you for submitting your sleep diary last Friday. I have examined all seven days, and the pattern is obvious. On school nights you go to bed at about half past midnight, and you rise at five. That allows you roughly four and a half hours of rest. A teenager of sixteen requires far more.

Your diary also reveals the effect. You fall asleep during lessons, you buy sweet drinks in the break, and you feel hungry an hour afterwards. Sugar lifts your energy for a brief period, then the effect disappears. Short sleep and sugar are working against each other here.

I suggest one experiment with you for a fortnight. Put your phone on the shelf by the door at ten o'clock, and read a novel until you feel sleepy. Please record the time you wake up, but ignore the rest. Please attend the clinic on Thursday during the long break. Kind regards, Nurse Dewi.
qs: Overall, why has Nurse Dewi written to Adit?
Sugar lifts energy, and the clinic can supply more advice.
Adit sleeps too little, so one habit should change.
Adit records his waking time, and the diary looks fine.
The clinic opens on Thursday, so the diary must be ready.

qs.evidence: I suggest one experiment with you for a fortnight.
qs.answer: Adit sleeps too little, so one habit should change.
qs.why: Isi utamanya: tidurnya kurang, terus nurse nawarin satu perubahan kecil.
qs.whyOthersFail: Gula dan jam klinik memang disebut, tapi keduanya rincian, dan teks nggak menaruh nasihat tambahan di klinik. Catatan jam bangun justru yang diminta, bukan yang udah beres. Kesiapan buku catatan buat hari Kamis nggak pernah ditulis.

qs: How much rest does the diary show on school nights?
Roughly seven hours and fifteen minutes
Roughly six hours and forty minutes
Roughly five hours and thirty minutes
Roughly four hours and thirty minutes

qs.evidence: That allows you roughly four and a half hours of rest.
qs.answer: Roughly four hours and thirty minutes
qs.why: “Four and a half hours” sama dengan empat jam tiga puluh menit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiga angka lain kedengeran wajar buat remaja, tapi teks nulis empat setengah jam: tidur setengah satu malam sampai jam lima. Nggak ada angka lima, enam, atau tujuh jam di email itu.

qs: What does "working against each other" mean here?
They cancel each other out, so no harm follows.
They take turns, and only one acts each day.
Each one makes the other problem worse.
They push his energy in the same direction.

qs.evidence: Short sleep and sugar are working against each other here.
qs.answer: Each one makes the other problem worse.
qs.why: Tidur kurang bikin dia ngantuk lalu beli minuman manis, dan gula itu balik lagi bikin lapar — saling memperburuk.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kalau saling meniadakan, nggak ada masalah yang dijelasin nurse; teks justru nyebut rangkaian efek buruk. “Gantian tiap hari” nggak ada di teks, dan mendorong ke arah yang sama malah kebalikan dari “against”.

qs: What does the nurse expect the phone rule to do?
Help Adit reach sleep earlier in the evening
Stop him buying sweet drinks in the break
Give him something to read for his lessons
Let the nurse check his diary more easily

qs.evidence: Put your phone on the shelf by the door at ten o'clock, and read a novel until you feel sleepy.
qs.answer: Help Adit reach sleep earlier in the evening
qs.why: Telepon ditaruh jauh jam sepuluh biar dia ngantuk lebih awal, bukan buat urusan lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: Minuman manis dibeli gara-gara ngantuk, bukan gara-gara telepon. Novel di aturan itu buat ngantuk, bukan tugas pelajaran. Buku catatannya cuma diminta nyatet jam bangun, bukan dipermudah buat nurse.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Adit buys three sweet drinks during every school break."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Adit buys three sweet drinks during every school break.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: You fall asleep during lessons, you buy sweet drinks in the break, and you feel hungry an hour afterwards.
qs.why: Teks cuma nyebut kamu beli minuman manis di jam istirahat; jumlahnya nggak pernah ditulis.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” butuh angka yang cocok di teks; “False” juga nggak bisa karena teks nggak nyebut jumlah lain.

author: Nurse Dewi
setting: a school clinic and a pupil home

title: Notice: Route 12 Changes for Four Weeks
text:
To all passengers: from Monday next week, Route 12 will not enter Melati Street. A crew is laying new water pipes there, and the road will be closed to buses for four weeks.

During this period, buses will turn left at the market and stop behind the sports hall instead. The new stop is about three hundred metres from the previous one. Each morning a member of staff will assist passengers there. Please allow ten additional minutes for your journey, especially in wet weather.

Tickets bought for the previous route remain valid, and no additional fare will be charged. Pupils who travel before seven may display their school card as usual. If you require assistance, ring the depot office between eight in the morning and four in the afternoon. You may also ask any driver on the route. Queues at the market may become longer during the evening rush. We apologize for the trouble while the crew completes the pipes.
qs: Overall, what does this notice tell passengers about Route 12?
New water pipes for the houses on Melati Street
A short change to Route 12 because of roadworks
Extra staff at the bus stop behind the sports hall
The rules for pupils who travel before seven

qs.evidence: A crew is laying new water pipes there, and the road will be closed to buses for four weeks.
qs.answer: A short change to Route 12 because of roadworks
qs.why: Jalan ditutup gara-gara pekerjaan pipa, jadi rutenya dialihkan sementara.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pipa air, petugas di pemberhentian baru, dan aturan murid pagi memang disebut, tapi ketiganya bagian kecil. Pengumumannya sendiri soal rute yang dialihkan selama empat pekan.

qs: Where will buses stop while Melati Street is closed?
At a temporary stop on Melati Street itself
Beside the market, where the buses turn left
Outside the depot office near the main road
In the space at the rear of the sports hall

qs.evidence: During this period, buses will turn left at the market and stop behind the sports hall instead.
qs.answer: In the space at the rear of the sports hall
qs.why: Bus muter ke kiri di pasar terus berhenti di belakang gedung olahraga.
qs.whyOthersFail: Melati Street justru ditutup buat bus. Pasar cuma tempat bus belok kiri, bukan tempat berhenti. Kantor depo hanya nomor telepon buat bantuan, nggak pernah jadi pemberhentian.

qs: What are passengers asked to do about time?
Set aside ten more minutes for the trip
Arrive at the stop ten minutes before departure
Ring the depot before four in the afternoon
Allow ten minutes more only in wet weather

qs.evidence: Please allow ten additional minutes for your journey, especially in wet weather.
qs.answer: Set aside ten more minutes for the trip
qs.why: “Allow ten extra minutes” artinya sisihin sepuluh menit tambahan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Datang sepuluh menit sebelum bus nggak pernah diminta. Nelepon depo itu buat minta bantuan, bukan soal waktu perjalanan. Dan tambahan sepuluh menit berlaku tiap hari, cuaca basah cuma ditekankan.

qs: Why will a member of staff be at the new stop?
Because tickets may have to be checked again there
Because the queue at the market might turn dangerous
Because some passengers may not know where to go
Because the pipe work leaves the pavement unsafe

qs.evidence: Each morning a member of staff will assist passengers there.
qs.answer: Because some passengers may not know where to go
qs.why: Pemberhentiannya baru dan tiga ratus meter dari yang lama, jadi petugas ada buat nunjukin arah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiket lama tetap sah dan nggak ada pemeriksaan ulang di teks. Antrean di pasar disebut cuma jadi lebih panjang, bukan berbahaya. Bahaya trotoar gara-gara pipa juga nggak pernah ditulis.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Passengers must pay a small extra fare during the four weeks."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Passengers must pay a small extra fare during the four weeks.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Tickets bought for the previous route remain valid, and no additional fare will be charged.
qs.why: Teks jelas bilang nggak ada biaya tambahan, jadi klaim ini kebalikannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” mustahil karena polaritasnya dibalik; “Not stated” nggak pas karena soal tarif justru ditulis.

author: City bus depot
setting: a city bus route and its stops

title: The Cheap Studio in a Bedroom
text:
Ten years ago, a young musician in Yogyakarta needed a studio, an engineer and a lot of money. Today the same person needs a laptop, a microphone and a quiet corner. Recording software has become cheap, and some of it costs nothing at all.

This change has two faces. On the good side, more voices reach an audience. A pupil can write a song on Sunday, record it on Monday and share it on Tuesday. Nobody has to ask a company for permission first.

On the other side, a bedroom is not built for sound. Traffic noise passes through windows, and hard walls make the voice sound thin. Musicians learn simple tricks. They hang a thick blanket behind the microphone, and they sing away from the centre of the room. Many of them also record after midnight. The result is not perfect, and listeners often hear the difference. Yet a rough song that exists beats a clean song that nobody records.
qs: Overall, what point does this text make about recording music at home?
Software is cheap, so home studios have begun to close.
A blanket helps, and a bedroom can beat any studio.
A musician can write and share a song in three days.
Home recording is easy now, but the sound has limits.

qs.evidence: The result is not perfect, and listeners often hear the difference.
qs.answer: Home recording is easy now, but the sound has limits.
qs.why: Dua sisi dibahas: gampang dan murah, tapi kualitas suaranya kalah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Harga perangkat lunak yang murah nggak bikin studio tutup menurut teks. Selimut cuma nurunin gema, jauh dari mengalahkan studio. Tiga hari itu contoh kecepatan, bukan simpulan tulisannya.

qs: Overall, what does a musician need today, according to this text?
A studio, an engineer and a large budget
A portable computer, a microphone and silence
A microphone, a blanket and a paid licence
A laptop, an engineer and a quiet corner

qs.evidence: Today the same person needs a laptop, a microphone and a quiet corner.
qs.answer: A portable computer, a microphone and silence
qs.why: “Laptop” itu komputer jinjing dan “quiet corner” itu tempat sepi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Studio plus perekayasa plus uang banyak itu kebutuhan sepuluh tahun lalu. Izin berbayar nggak pernah disebut; teks malah bilang nggak perlu minta izin perusahaan. Perekayasa suara juga udah nggak masuk daftar sekarang.

qs: What does "thin" mean in the last paragraph?
quiet enough to ignore
spread out across the room
weak and lacking fullness
narrow like a small window

qs.evidence: Traffic noise passes through windows, and hard walls make the voice sound thin.
qs.answer: weak and lacking fullness
qs.why: Yang dibahas mutu suara, jadi “thin” di sini artinya tipis alias kurang penuh.
qs.whyOthersFail: Suara pelan sampai nggak kedengeran bukan soalnya; masalahnya mutu, bukan volume. “Menyebar di ruangan” dan “sempit seperti jendela” mengambil arti tebal-tipis benda, padahal yang dinilai warna suara.

qs: Why do many musicians record after midnight?
Because the street outside is much quieter then
Because free software runs faster late at night
Because most listeners open new songs at night
Because hard walls sound better in cool air

qs.evidence: Many of them also record after midnight.
qs.answer: Because the street outside is much quieter then
qs.why: Masalah utamanya suara lalu lintas dari jendela, dan jalanan paling sepi lewat tengah malam.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kecepatan perangkat lunak nggak pernah dikaitin sama jam. Jam dengar pendengar juga nggak dibahas. Dinding keras itu masalah tetap di teks, dan udara dingin nggak disebut bisa memperbaikinya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "A few recording programs can be used without paying anything."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: A few recording programs can be used without paying anything.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Recording software has become cheap, and some of it costs nothing at all.
qs.why: Teks bilang sebagian perangkatnya “costs nothing at all”, jadi ada yang bisa dipakai gratis.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” butuh proposisi yang dibalik dan nggak ada; “Not stated” salah karena harga disebut di kalimat itu.

author: Music pages
setting: bedrooms used as studios in Yogyakarta

title: The Night the Canal Rose
text:
One night in the rainy season, the rain over Semarang did not stop for eleven hours. At nine in the evening, the water in the canal behind Pak Hasan's shop was still low. By eleven it was level with the pavement, and by midnight it stood inside his door.

Pak Hasan did not wait for help. The lane outside was silent. He moved the rice, the sugar and the boxes of soap to the top shelf. Then he switched off the electricity at the wall, took his neighbour's ladder and carried his cat to the flat roof. From there he could hear the water moving under the floor. Nobody else was awake.

The rain ceased at four in the morning, and the canal fell quickly. Nobody expected the storm to pass so gently. By dawn the damage was surprisingly small. When Pak Hasan came down at six, most of the shop was wet, but almost none of the stock was ruined. His neighbours copied his method during the storm three weeks later. The council cleaned the canal that month, and the shop has stayed dry since then.
qs: Overall, what does this story show about the night the canal rose?
Eleven hours of rain filled the canal behind a shop.
A council team cleaned the canal later that month.
Fast action at night spared a shop from real loss.
Neighbours copied a shopkeeper during a later storm.

qs.evidence: When Pak Hasan came down at six, most of the shop was wet, but almost none of the stock was ruined.
qs.answer: Fast action at night spared a shop from real loss.
qs.why: Barangnya nyaris utuh gara-gara dia gerak cepat malam itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Hujan sebelas jam, kerja petugas kota, dan tetangga yang niru semuanya ada di cerita, tapi ketiganya bagian. Intinya tindakan cepat Pak Hasan yang bikin kerugiannya kecil.

qs: What did Pak Hasan do before he climbed to the roof?
He carried the cat up the ladder first.
He cut the power supply at the wall.
He woke the neighbours in the quiet lane.
He moved the boxes down to the floor.

qs.evidence: Then he switched off the electricity at the wall, took his neighbour's ladder and carried his cat to the flat roof.
qs.answer: He cut the power supply at the wall.
qs.why: “Switched off the electricity” sama dengan mutus aliran listrik di dinding.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kucingnya dibawa sesudah listrik dimatikan, jadi urutannya kebalik. Teks bilang gang di luar sepi dan nggak ada orang lain yang bangun. Barang justru dinaikin ke rak atas, bukan diturunin ke lantai.

qs: When did the water reach the level of the pavement?
By eleven o'clock that evening
Shortly before nine that evening
At about midnight that night
Not until four in the morning

qs.evidence: By eleven it was level with the pavement, and by midnight it stood inside his door.
qs.answer: By eleven o'clock that evening
qs.why: Jam sebelas malam air udah rata sama trotoar; tengah malam baru masuk pintu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jam sembilan airnya masih rendah. Tengah malam itu saat air masuk pintu, udah lewat trotoar. Jam empat pagi hujan berhenti dan airnya turun, bukan naik.

qs: Why did the neighbours copy his method?
Because the council told the street to prepare
Because he warned them at nine that evening
Because their shops stand lower than his
Because his goods survived while the water rose

qs.evidence: His neighbours copied his method during the storm three weeks later.
qs.answer: Because his goods survived while the water rose
qs.why: Caranya kelihatan berhasil: hampir semua stok selamat, jadi tetangganya niru.
qs.whyOthersFail: Petugas kota cuma bersihin kanal, nggak nyuruh siapa-siapa siap-siap. Malam itu nggak ada yang dibangunin; gangnya sepi. Ketinggian toko tetangga nggak pernah disebut di teks.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The canal emptied fast once the rain had ended."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The canal emptied fast once the rain had ended.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The rain ceased at four in the morning, and the canal fell quickly.
qs.why: “Fell quickly” sama maksudnya sama “emptied fast”, dan waktunya juga sesudah hujan berhenti.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” nggak pas karena nggak ada bagian yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena turunnya air ditulis jelas.

author: Local reporter
setting: a small shop beside a canal in Semarang

title: Report: Water Bottles Beat the Tuck Shop
text:
The health committee has finished its two-month study of drinking habits in Years 7 to 9. In the first week, only 84 of 320 pupils brought a bottle of water to school. Two months later the number had risen to 213.

The committee took three steps. It installed two new taps beside the hall. Form teachers agreed to remind their classes every Monday. The committee also printed a simple notice for every door. Members counted the empty bottles in the bins each Friday afternoon.

Sales of sweet drinks in the tuck shop fell by about a third during the same period. Pak Yusuf, who runs the shop, was not pleased at first. He now sells cold fruit and small packets of nuts, and he admits the change has cost him little. The committee will report to the head teacher next term. Its main request is one more tap near the sports field, where pupils queue longest.
qs: Overall, what change does this report describe in pupils' drinking habits?
The fall in sweet drink sales at the tuck shop
The new taps that the committee put beside the hall
A successful push to get pupils drinking water
A request for one more tap near the sports field

qs.evidence: The health committee has finished its two-month study of drinking habits in Years 7 to 9.
qs.answer: A successful push to get pupils drinking water
qs.why: Laporannya soal usaha bikin murid minum air, plus hasil angkanya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Turunnya penjualan minuman manis, keran baru di samping aula, dan permintaan keran tambahan semuanya benar, tapi masing-masing satu bagian laporan. Pokoknya usaha yang berhasil bikin murid minum air.

qs: How many pupils brought water at the end of the study?
Two hundred and thirteen pupils
Three hundred and twenty pupils
One hundred and thirty pupils
Eighty-four of the pupils

qs.evidence: Two months later the number had risen to 213.
qs.answer: Two hundred and thirteen pupils
qs.why: Angka 213 ditulis dengan kata di kunci; 320 itu jumlah semua murid, bukan pembawa botol.
qs.whyOthersFail: 320 itu jumlah seluruh murid Kelas 7-9, bukan pembawa botol. 84 angka pekan pertama, jadi salah waktu. Angka seratus tiga puluh nggak pernah muncul di laporan.

qs: What did members do every Friday?
They counted the pupils who carried bottles
They checked the rubbish for used bottles
They reminded every form about drinking water
They put a new notice on every door

qs.evidence: Members counted the empty bottles in the bins each Friday afternoon.
qs.answer: They checked the rubbish for used bottles
qs.why: Tiap Jumat mereka ngitung botol kosong di tempat sampah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang dihitung botol di tempat sampah, bukan muridnya. Pengingat ke tiap kelas kerjaan guru dan jatuhnya hari Senin. Notice di pintu dicetak sekali, bukan kegiatan tiap Jumat.

qs: What can we infer about Pak Yusuf?
He now earns more than he did before.
He still hopes the taps will be removed.
He has stopped selling drinks in the shop.
He has fitted his shop to the new habit.

qs.evidence: He now sells cold fruit and small packets of nuts, and he admits the change has cost him little.
qs.answer: He has fitted his shop to the new habit.
qs.why: Dia ganti barang jualan dan ngaku ruginya kecil, jadi dia nyesuain diri.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks cuma bilang perubahan itu “cost him little”, bukan untungnya naik. Dia kesal di awal, tapi nggak ada permintaan keran dicabut. Penjualan minuman manis turun sepertiga, bukan berhenti.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The committee asks for another tap beside the school hall."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The committee asks for another tap beside the school hall.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Its main request is one more tap near the sports field, where pupils queue longest.
qs.why: Permintaannya keran baru deket lapangan olahraga, bukan deket aula; tempatnya ditukar.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena lokasinya beda; “Not stated” nggak pas karena permintaan keran memang ditulis.

topic: a school study of drinking habits
author: Health committee
setting: a lower secondary school and its tuck shop

title: Reading a Station Board in Ten Seconds
text:
A busy station can appear like a wall of letters and figures. In fact, every board follows the same order, and ten seconds are enough once you know it. Regular travellers notice the pattern immediately.

Start at the left, where the departure time appears. Boards show the time a train leaves, not the time it arrives. Next appears the final destination of the line. Your own station may be halfway along, so examine the small list under the name. The platform number is on the right, and it changes more often than anything else. Experienced passengers ignore the crowd and check this number twice.

The last column carries short remarks: on time, delayed, or a single word such as "cancelled". If the space is empty, nothing unusual has occurred. Travellers who plan a tight change should watch this column, because ten lost minutes may cost an hour later. Staff at small stations still write the boards by hand, so a quiet announcement is sometimes faster than the screen.
qs: Overall, what does this text teach readers about station boards?
Why platform numbers change so often
How staff at small stations write the boards
How to read the parts of a station board fast
Which remarks the last column can carry

qs.evidence: In fact, every board follows the same order, and ten seconds are enough once you know it.
qs.answer: How to read the parts of a station board fast
qs.why: Artikelnya nunjukin urutan kolom papan biar cepat kebaca.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nomor peron, tulisan tangan petugas, dan isi kolom catatan memang dibahas, tapi ketiganya bagian dari penjelasan. Pokok artikelnya cara membaca papan dalam sepuluh detik.

qs: Overall, which time does every station board display?
The moment a train pulls in
The moment the platform is announced
The moment a train sets off
The moment the board was written

qs.evidence: Boards show the time a train leaves, not the time it arrives.
qs.answer: The moment a train sets off
qs.why: Yang dipampang jam keberangkatan, bukan jam kedatangan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jam kedatangan justru yang teks bilang bukan; itu kebalikannya. Papan nggak nulis kapan peron diumumkan, cuma nomornya. Jam petugas nulis papan juga nggak pernah dipampang.

qs: How can you check that a train stops at your own station?
look at the small list under the final destination
read the number printed on the right of the board
check the remarks written in the final column
compare the time on the left with your watch

qs.evidence: Your own station may be halfway along, so examine the small list under the name.
qs.answer: look at the small list under the final destination
qs.why: Stasiunmu bisa di tengah jalur, jadi lihat daftar kecil di bawah nama tujuan akhir.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nomor di kanan itu peron, dan kolom catatan soal keterlambatan; dua-duanya nggak nunjukin stasiun tengah. Jam di kiri cuma waktu keberangkatan.

qs: Why should a passenger with a tight change watch the last column?
Because a small delay can spoil the whole plan
Because the column names the next platform
Because staff update it before the other columns
Because an empty space means a late train

qs.evidence: Travellers who plan a tight change should watch this column, because ten lost minutes may cost an hour later.
qs.answer: Because a small delay can spoil the whole plan
qs.why: Telat sepuluh menit bisa jadi kehilangan satu jam, jadi rencana sambungannya rusak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nomor peron ada di kolom kanan, bukan di kolom catatan. Urutan petugas mengisi kolom nggak pernah ditulis. Kolom kosong justru berarti nggak ada yang aneh, bukan tanda telat.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Platform numbers change often because trains arrive late."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Platform numbers change often because trains arrive late.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: The platform number is on the right, and it changes more often than anything else.
qs.why: Teks cuma bilang nomor peron paling sering ganti; alasannya nggak pernah dijelasin.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” butuh sebab yang tertulis dan nggak ada; “False” juga nggak bisa karena teks nggak nyebut sebab lain.

topic: how to read a railway departure board
author: Travel guide desk
setting: a busy railway station

title: Email: Permission for the Class Account
text:
Dear Mr Bayu, I am writing on behalf of the media team in Year 11. We manage the class account that publishes photographs from school events. Last week a parent complained about a picture of her daughter, and we removed it within an hour.

The team would like to prevent similar problems. Before an event, we shall pass round a short form. Pupils may tick a box if they prefer to avoid photographs. During the event, one member will hold the list and examine faces before we publish anything.

The system requires your approval, because the account carries the school name. We also need a locked cupboard for the printed forms. May we present the plan at the staff meeting on Tuesday? It should take five minutes, and my deputy can answer questions about the software. Yours sincerely, Sari, media team leader.
qs: Overall, why has Sari written to Mr Bayu?
To explain how the team removed one picture
To book five minutes at Tuesday's staff meeting
To request approval for a rule about photographs
To ask for a locked cupboard for the forms

qs.evidence: The team would like to prevent similar problems.
qs.answer: To request approval for a rule about photographs
qs.why: Sari nawarin aturan baru soal foto dan minta izin guru buat jalanin.
qs.whyOthersFail: Penghapusan foto itu latar belakang, bukan tujuan surat. Waktu lima menit di rapat dan lemari terkunci memang diminta, tapi keduanya menempel pada permintaan utama: izin buat aturan foto.

qs: What did the team do after the complaint?
They deleted the photograph within an hour.
They asked the parent to sign a short form.
They closed the account until Tuesday's meeting.
They passed the picture to Mr Bayu at once.

qs.evidence: Last week a parent complained about a picture of her daughter, and we removed it within an hour.
qs.answer: They deleted the photograph within an hour.
qs.why: “Removed it within an hour” artinya fotonya dihapus dalam satu jam.
qs.whyOthersFail: Formulir itu buat murid, bukan buat orang tua tanda tangan. Akun kelas nggak pernah ditutup di teks. Foto itu dihapus, bukan diserahkan ke Mr Bayu.

qs: What will pupils do with the form?
Hand it to a parent for a signature
Mark a box to refuse being photographed
Give it to the member who holds the list
Keep it in the locked cupboard themselves

qs.evidence: Pupils may tick a box if they prefer to avoid photographs.
qs.answer: Mark a box to refuse being photographed
qs.why: “Tick a box” itu nyentang kotak, dan tujuannya biar nggak difoto.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tanda tangan orang tua nggak diminta di rencana ini. Anggota tim yang pegang daftar bertugas saat acara, bukan penerima formulir. Lemari terkunci dipakai tim buat menyimpan, bukan murid.

qs: Why does Sari ask for the teacher's approval?
Because a parent has asked for a written rule
Because the software needs a teacher's password
Because the account represents the whole school
Because only staff may hold the printed forms

qs.evidence: The system requires your approval, because the account carries the school name.
qs.answer: Because the account represents the whole school
qs.why: Akun itu bawa nama sekolah, jadi keputusannya nggak bisa cuma di tangan murid.
qs.whyOthersFail: Orang tua mengeluh soal satu foto, bukan minta aturan tertulis. Kata sandi perangkat lunak nggak pernah disebut. Formulir cetak disimpan di lemari, tapi teks nggak bilang cuma guru yang boleh pegang.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Sari wants to present the plan at a meeting on Thursday."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Sari wants to present the plan at a meeting on Thursday.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: May we present the plan at the staff meeting on Tuesday?
qs.why: Dia minta waktu di rapat hari Selasa, bukan Kamis; harinya ditukar.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena harinya beda; “Not stated” nggak pas karena hari rapatnya ditulis.

topic: consent for photographs on a school account
author: Sari
setting: a Year 11 media team and a teacher

title: What Ten Minutes of Walking Does
text:
Doctors often recommend thirty minutes of exercise a day. For a busy pupil that sounds impossible, so many people give up before they begin. Recent studies suggest a gentler approach, and the numbers are clear. Three walks of ten minutes produce almost the same benefit as one long session.

The reason lies in the blood. A short walk raises the heart rate, moves fresh blood to the muscles and clears sugar from the body. The effect lasts for roughly two hours. After that the body slows down again, which is why several small doses beat a single effort.

The habit is easy to build. Walk to the shop instead of using the motorbike, and leave the bus one stop early. Climb the stairs while the lift stands empty. None of these decisions feels like sport, and none requires special clothes. A month later, most walkers report better sleep and steadier moods.
qs: Overall, what point does this text make about short walks?
A short walk clears sugar, so one walk a day may suffice.
Doctors advise thirty minutes, and shorter walks often fail.
Short walks, repeated often, deliver most of the gain.
Walkers sleep better, and their weight falls in a month.

qs.evidence: Three walks of ten minutes produce almost the same benefit as one long session.
qs.answer: Short walks, repeated often, deliver most of the gain.
qs.why: Inti teksnya: jalan pendek tapi sering hasilnya nyaris sama kayak sekali lama.
qs.whyOthersFail: Satu kali jalan sehari nggak cukup menurut teks; yang penting diulang beberapa kali. Jalan pendek juga nggak disebut gagal, malah dianjurkan. Tidur membaik memang ditulis, tapi soal turun berat badan sebulan nggak ada.

qs: How long does the effect of a short walk last?
For about twenty minutes afterwards
For about one hour afterwards
For the rest of the school day
For about two hours afterwards

qs.evidence: The effect lasts for roughly two hours.
qs.answer: For about two hours afterwards
qs.why: “Roughly two hours” itu kira-kira dua jam.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dua puluh menit dan satu jam kedengeran wajar, tapi teks nulis kira-kira dua jam. “Sisa hari sekolah” malah bertentangan, karena teks bilang badan melambat lagi sesudah dua jam.

qs: What does "doses" mean in the second paragraph?
measured amounts of liquid medicine
readings of the heart rate
short rests between walks
separate portions of activity

qs.evidence: After that the body slows down again, which is why several small doses beat a single effort.
qs.answer: separate portions of activity
qs.why: Yang dihitung di sini bagian-bagian jalan kaki, bukan obat; makanya “doses” artinya porsi kegiatan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Arti obat memang arti biasa “dose”, tapi di kalimat itu yang dibagi-bagi kegiatan jalan. Denyut jantung cuma efek, bukan yang dihitung. Istirahat antar jalan nggak pernah disebut teks.

qs: Why does the writer mention the lift?
To show a chance for exercise hidden in the day
To warn that lifts often break down in schools
To prove that stairs are safer than lifts
To explain why pupils feel tired in the afternoon

qs.evidence: Climb the stairs while the lift stands empty.
qs.answer: To show a chance for exercise hidden in the day
qs.why: Naik tangga waktu lift kosong itu contoh olahraga yang nyempil di kegiatan biasa.
qs.whyOthersFail: Lift rusak nggak pernah dibahas. Teks juga nggak bandingin keamanan tangga dan lift. Rasa lelah sore hari nggak dikaitin sama lift di teks mana pun.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "A brief walk speeds up the heartbeat."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: A brief walk speeds up the heartbeat.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: A short walk raises the heart rate, moves fresh blood to the muscles and clears sugar from the body.
qs.why: “Raises the heart rate” sama maksudnya sama detak jantung jadi lebih cepat.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” nggak bisa karena nggak ada bagian yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena efek ini ditulis di kalimat itu.

author: Health pages
setting: daily routines of busy pupils

title: A Wrong Junction on the Way to Toba
text:
Last dry season, Nadia and her cousin boarded the night bus towards Lake Toba. The driver dropped them at a junction at four in the morning, and the following bus was due at six. There was no shelter, only a closed stall and a dog asleep on the concrete step.

Nadia examined her phone. The battery showed nine per cent, and there was no signal in the valley. Instead of waiting in the dark, the two girls walked towards a light. It came out of a food stall two hundred metres away. The owner was already heating water for coffee, and she invited them inside.

By six o'clock the bus had not appeared. The owner mentioned that the service had changed a month earlier; the morning bus now left from the market. Her son gave them a lift on his motorbike, one at a time, and they reached the market at seven. Nadia admits the wrong junction taught her to ask a local resident first.
qs: Overall, what does this story show about the journey towards Lake Toba?
A dead phone left two girls without any help at all.
The bus dropped them early, and the stall stayed closed.
A local person solved a problem the timetable created.
A motorbike ride is faster than the morning bus is.

qs.evidence: Nadia admits the wrong junction taught her to ask a local resident first.
qs.answer: A local person solved a problem the timetable created.
qs.why: Yang nyelametin mereka informasi dari pemilik warung setempat, bukan jadwal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Baterainya tinggal sembilan persen, bukan mati, dan mereka justru dapat pertolongan. Warung yang tutup itu yang di simpang; warung dua ratus meter jauhnya malah buka. Tumpangan motor cuma jalan keluar, bukan perbandingan kecepatan.

qs: Why did the girls leave the junction?
Because the closed stall would not open
Because a dog on the step frightened them
Because they saw a light further along
Because the driver pointed them to the market

qs.evidence: Instead of waiting in the dark, the two girls walked towards a light.
qs.answer: Because they saw a light further along
qs.why: Mereka jalan ke arah cahaya, bukan nunggu di gelap.
qs.whyOthersFail: Warung tutup cuma latar, bukan alasan mereka pergi. Anjingnya tidur dan nggak bikin takut. Pengemudi bus cuma nurunin mereka di simpang, nggak nunjukin arah pasar.

qs: What happened straight after six o'clock?
Her son drove both girls to the market at once
The two girls walked back to the dark junction
The phone battery went flat in the valley
The stall owner explained a change to the route

qs.evidence: The owner mentioned that the service had changed a month earlier; the morning bus now left from the market.
qs.answer: The stall owner explained a change to the route
qs.why: Pas busnya nggak datang jam enam, pemilik warung ngejelasin rutenya udah pindah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Anaknya nganter satu-satu, bukan berdua sekaligus, dan itu sesudah penjelasan. Mereka nggak balik ke simpang. Baterai habis total nggak pernah ditulis di teks.

qs: Why did Nadia not telephone for advice?
Because her battery had already gone flat
Because the valley gave her phone no reception
Because she had nobody's number with her
Because the stall owner asked her to wait

qs.evidence: The battery showed nine per cent, and there was no signal in the valley.
qs.answer: Because the valley gave her phone no reception
qs.why: Baterainya masih ada sedikit, tapi di lembah itu nggak ada sinyal sama sekali.
qs.whyOthersFail: Baterainya masih sembilan persen, jadi belum habis. Daftar nomor di teleponnya nggak pernah dibahas. Pemilik warung malah ngajak masuk dan ngasih kabar, bukan nyuruh nunggu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The son carried both girls on the motorbike together."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The son carried both girls on the motorbike together.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Her son gave them a lift on his motorbike, one at a time, and they reached the market at seven.
qs.why: Teks bilang mereka diangkut satu per satu, jadi klaim “bareng” itu ngebalik jumlahnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena jumlah penumpang tiap perjalanan beda; “Not stated” nggak pas karena caranya ditulis jelas.

topic: a night journey that went wrong
author: Travel diary
setting: a roadside junction near Lake Toba

title: Report: The Rubbish Audit in Block C
text:
The environment club spent three Fridays weighing the rubbish from Block C. The result surprised the teachers: the club collected 46 kilograms in total. Plastic bottles and cups from the tuck shop made up 19 kilograms. Only 6 kilograms could not be recycled at all.

The club showed the figures at assembly with a simple chart. Members then asked for two changes. They wanted a sorting station near the stairs and a discount for pupils with their own cup. The head teacher approved the sorting station immediately. The discount, she said, must wait for the shop's agreement.

Since the station opened, the club has weighed the rubbish twice more. The plastic share has fallen to about a quarter, though the total weight has barely moved. Members admit that some pupils still drop cups in the wrong bin. Two volunteers now stand beside the station during the long break.
qs: Overall, what does this report tell readers about the rubbish in Block C?
The weight of plastic and the price of a new cup
The findings of a rubbish study and what followed
The chart at assembly and the vote that came after
The work of two volunteers and the shop's agreement

qs.evidence: The environment club spent three Fridays weighing the rubbish from Block C.
qs.answer: The findings of a rubbish study and what followed
qs.why: Laporannya nyajikan hasil penimbangan sampah plus tindakan sesudahnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Berat plastik disebut, tapi harga cangkir nggak pernah ditulis. Grafik di upacara ada, pemungutan suara nggak. Dua relawan memang berjaga, dan persetujuan toko masih ditunggu, jadi keduanya cuma potongan cerita.

qs: How much of the rubbish could not be recycled?
Nineteen kilograms of the load
Six kilograms of the whole load
Forty-six kilograms, the whole load
About a quarter of the load

qs.evidence: Only 6 kilograms could not be recycled at all.
qs.answer: Six kilograms of the whole load
qs.why: Angka 6 kilogram itu bagian yang nggak bisa didaur ulang; 19 dan 46 angka lain.
qs.whyOthersFail: 19 kilogram itu botol dan gelas plastik, 46 kilogram total semua sampah. “Sekitar seperempat” angka plastik sesudah stasiun pemilahan dibuka, bukan sampah yang nggak bisa didaur ulang.

qs: What did the head teacher decide about the discount?
She approved it with the sorting station
She refused it because of the cost
She left it to the environment club
She delayed it until the shop agrees

qs.evidence: The discount, she said, must wait for the shop's agreement.
qs.answer: She delayed it until the shop agrees
qs.why: “Must wait for the shop’s agreement” artinya ditunda sampai pemilik toko setuju.
qs.whyOthersFail: Yang langsung disetujui cuma stasiun pemilahan, bukan potongan harga. Alasan biaya nggak pernah disebut. Keputusannya juga nggak dilempar ke klub lingkungan.

qs: Why do two volunteers stand beside the station?
Because mistakes with the bins continue
Because the station stands too far from Block C
Because the club must weigh the rubbish again
Because the shop has stopped selling paper cups

qs.evidence: Members admit that some pupils still drop cups in the wrong bin.
qs.answer: Because mistakes with the bins continue
qs.why: Masih ada murid yang salah taruh gelas, jadi ada yang jaga di sebelah stasiun.

title: The Battery Rule Everyone Repeats
text:
Ask ten people how to treat a phone battery, and you will hear ten different rules. The most popular one is old advice: let the battery empty completely, then charge it to a hundred per cent. That rule belonged to the batteries of the nineteen-nineties, which suffered from a memory effect.

Modern phones use lithium cells, and they prefer the middle. Engineers who design them suggest a range between twenty and eighty per cent. Deep discharges and long nights at full charge both shorten the life of the cell. Heat does even more damage, so a phone left in the sun ages faster than one used all day.

None of this means you should watch the figure constantly. A battery is a part that wears out, like a tyre. Sensible habits simply delay the moment when you must replace it.
qs: Overall, what point does this text make about phone batteries?
Why heat harms a cell and how the memory effect began
How old batteries lost capacity and why tyres wear out
How modern batteries differ from the old advice
Why a battery wears out and when to replace the phone

qs.evidence: Modern phones use lithium cells, and they prefer the middle.
qs.answer: How modern batteries differ from the old advice
qs.why: Teks bandingin aturan lama sama sifat baterai model sekarang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Panas dan memory effect memang dibahas, tapi asal-usul memory effect nggak diceritain. Ban cuma perbandingan, bukan topik. Waktu penggantian telepon juga nggak pernah disebut.

qs: What harms a lithium cell, according to the text?
Charging it briefly several times a day
Making long calls throughout the whole day
Keeping the charge between twenty and eighty
Leaving it full overnight or letting it empty

qs.evidence: Deep discharges and long nights at full charge both shorten the life of the cell.
qs.answer: Leaving it full overnight or letting it empty
qs.why: Dua hal yang disebut merusak: dikosongin habis dan dibiarin penuh semalaman.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ngecas sebentar-sebentar justru bikin baterai tetap di tengah, yang disukai teks. Pemakaian sepanjang hari malah disebut lebih ringan daripada kena matahari. Rentang dua puluh sampai delapan puluh itu saran perekayasa, bukan penyebab rusak.

It matters less than a deep discharge
It only harms the batteries of old phones
It wears a battery out more quickly
It has little effect on a lithium cell

qs.evidence: Heat does even more damage, so a phone left in the sun ages faster than one used all day.
qs.answer: It wears a battery out more quickly
qs.why: Panas bikin baterai “ages faster”, alias tua lebih cepat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang panas merusak lebih parah daripada dikosongin habis, jadi dua opsi yang meremehkannya berlawanan. Panas juga nggak dibatasi ke telepon lama; contohnya justru telepon yang dijemur sekarang.

qs: According to the article, what will happen to any phone battery in the end?
It will wear out and have to be replaced.

It will keep its full capacity near fifty per cent.
It will recover once the memory effect is cleared.

qs.evidence: Sensible habits simply delay the moment when you must replace it.
qs.answer: It will wear out and have to be replaced.
qs.why: Teks menyebut kebiasaan yang masuk akal hanya menunda saat baterai harus diganti, jadi baterai pasti aus pada akhirnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Panas mempercepat kerusakan, tapi bukan satu-satunya penyebab. Rentang dua puluh sampai delapan puluh persen memperpanjang umur, bukan membuat kapasitasnya utuh terus. Memory effect itu masalah baterai tahun sembilan puluhan, bukan sel litium sekarang.

True
False

qs.answer: True

title: Notice: Free Eye Tests in the Sports Hall
text:
The district clinic will run free eye tests in the sports hall on Wednesday and Thursday next week. Every pupil in Years 7 to 12 may attend, and no charge applies. The nurses can examine about sixty pupils an hour.

Please note three points. First, bring your glasses if you already own a pair, because the team wants to measure the current lenses. Second, the test includes drops for some pupils, and those drops blur the vision for roughly two hours. Do not plan a maths examination or a long ride home straight afterwards. Third, pupils under fourteen need a signed note from a parent.

Classes will continue as normal, and teachers will release pupils in small groups. A list of times appears on the notice board tomorrow. If your family has already booked a private test this term, tell your form teacher. Your name will then move to the reserve list.

title: Why the Forecast Says Sixty Per Cent
text:
A weather app rarely promises rain. It offers a number instead: sixty per cent for Thursday afternoon. Many readers treat the figure as a measure of strength, and they expect heavy rain rather than light rain. The number means something different.

Forecasters test the same model many times, changing the starting weather a little each time. If rain appears in sixty tests out of a hundred, the forecast reports sixty per cent. The figure describes confidence, not volume: it shows how sure the forecasters are, not how much rain will fall. A short shower and a long storm can share the same percentage.

The area matters too. Most services work out the chance for a whole district, so the rain may fall on one village and miss the next. This is why a dry afternoon does not prove the forecast wrong. Farmers and event planners read the number as a warning about risk. Their rule is simple: at sixty per cent, carry the cover.
qs: Overall, what point does this text make about a rain percentage?
Apps report for a district, so the figure means little.
Sixty per cent means heavy rain, not a light shower.
Farmers carry a cover, and planners cancel the event.
A rain percentage shows confidence, not the amount.

qs.evidence: The figure describes confidence, not volume
qs.answer: A rain percentage shows confidence, not the amount.
qs.why: Angka itu ngukur seberapa yakin ramalannya, bukan seberapa banyak hujannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Hitungan per distrik nggak bikin angkanya tak berguna; teks tetap menyebutnya peringatan risiko. Anggapan hujan lebat justru salah baca yang diluruskan. Petani bawa penutup, tapi pembatalan acara nggak pernah ditulis.

qs: How do forecasters work out a figure such as sixty per cent?
they run the same model again and again with small changes
they compare the forecasts published by several services
they measure the rain that fell over the last few days
they count how many villages lie inside the district

qs.evidence: Forecasters test the same model many times, changing the starting weather a little each time.
qs.answer: they run the same model again and again with small changes
qs.why: Model yang sama dijalanin berkali-kali dengan kondisi awal yang beda sedikit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak nyebut penggabungan ramalan beberapa layanan. Hujan beberapa hari terakhir juga nggak diukur. Jumlah desa cuma muncul buat menjelaskan luas wilayah, bukan cara menghitung angkanya.

qs: What does "volume" mean in the second paragraph?
the loudness of rain on a roof
the quantity of water that falls
the size of the whole district
the level of trust in the forecast model

qs.evidence: it shows how sure the forecasters are, not how much rain will fall
qs.answer: the quantity of water that falls
qs.why: Yang dilawankan sama “confidence” itu banyaknya hujan, jadi “volume” di sini soal jumlah air.
qs.whyOthersFail: Arti “volume” sebagai kerasnya bunyi memang lazim, tapi di kalimat itu yang dibandingkan jumlah hujan. Luas distrik dibahas di paragraf lain. Tingkat keyakinan justru lawan katanya, yaitu “confidence”.

qs: Why can a dry afternoon still fit a sixty per cent forecast?
Because the app may change the number every hour
Because the shower may land somewhere else nearby
Because a percentage might refer to the whole week
Because forecasters ignore very light showers

qs.evidence: Most services work out the chance for a whole district, so the rain may fall on one village and miss the next.
qs.answer: Because the shower may land somewhere else nearby
qs.why: Ramalannya buat satu distrik, jadi hujannya bisa jatuh di desa sebelah.
qs.whyOthersFail: Pembaruan tiap jam nggak pernah disebut. Angkanya buat satu sore tertentu, bukan sepekan. Teks juga nggak bilang hujan ringan diabaikan; hujan ringan dan badai bisa sama persentasenya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The national weather office recommends the sixty per cent rule."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The national weather office recommends the sixty per cent rule.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Their rule is simple: at sixty per cent, carry the cover.
qs.why: Aturan itu dipakai petani dan penyelenggara acara; teks nggak pernah nyebut lembaga mana yang nyaranin.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” butuh sumber yang tertulis; “False” juga nggak bisa karena teks nggak nyangkal saran lembaga.

title: Report: The Phone Box Trial in Year 8
text:
For six weeks, every Year 8 class placed its phones in a locked box during lessons. The trial began after teachers counted forty interruptions in a single week. Pupils collected their phones again at the end of the day.

The results were mixed. Teachers recorded far fewer interruptions, and three classes finished their reading tasks earlier than usual. Yet twelve pupils complained that they could not tell their families about changes to the pick-up time. Two parents supported them in writing.

The council of pupils has proposed a compromise. Phones would stay in the box, but a monitor would carry one shared handset for urgent calls. The school will test this version after the holiday. Ms Lina, who leads the trial, admits the idea needs careful rules. "A shared phone can become a new interruption," she said. The council will report its findings to the parents' meeting in November.

The forty interruptions and the twelve pupils who wrote
A phone trial, its results and a proposed change
The complaint about pick-up times and the new handset

qs.whyOthersFail: Empat puluh gangguan benar, tapi yang menulis dua orang tua, bukan dua belas murid. Keluhan penjemputan ada, dan telepon bersama masih usulan. Peringatan Ms Lina dan kotak terkunci pun cuma bagian laporan.

title: The Truth About Skipping Breakfast
text:
Every year a magazine announces that breakfast is the most important meal, and every year another one denies it. The honest answer depends on the person. Studies that follow thousands of adults find no simple rule. Some people eat at seven and feel strong, while others feel sick before nine.

What matters more is the whole day. A pupil who skips breakfast and then buys fried snacks at ten has saved nothing. A pupil who skips breakfast and eats a proper lunch may feel perfectly well. Hunger itself is not the enemy; the real problem is a bad choice made in a hurry.

Two groups should be careful. Young athletes who train in the morning need fuel before exercise, or they lose strength in the second half. Pupils who take medicine with food must follow the instructions on the packet. For everyone else, the sensible plan is simple. Notice your own energy, and judge breakfast by how your afternoon goes.
qs: Overall, what point does this text make about skipping breakfast?
Skipping breakfast leads to snacks, and marks then fall.
Breakfast helps some people but not others.
Magazines agree each year, and their advice is safe.
Every pupil should eat lunch at noon, whatever happens.

qs.evidence: The honest answer depends on the person.
qs.answer: Breakfast helps some people but not others.
qs.why: Jawabannya tergantung orangnya, bukan satu aturan buat semua.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jajan gorengan disebut, tapi nilai yang turun nggak pernah ditulis. Majalah malah saling bertentangan tiap tahun. Makan siang yang layak cuma satu pilihan buat yang melewatkan sarapan, bukan aturan buat semua.

qs: What must pupils who take medicine do?
Eat breakfast at seven each morning
Ask a magazine for the safe hour
Do what the label tells them
Take the tablet after a proper lunch

qs.answer: Do what the label tells them
qs.why: Petunjuk di kemasan wajib diikuti, jadi jawabannya ikut label.
qs.whyOthersFail: Jam tujuh cuma contoh orang yang cocok sarapan pagi. Majalah bukan sumber aturan obat menurut teks. Makan siang yang layak dibahas untuk murid yang melewatkan sarapan, bukan untuk aturan obat.

qs: What does "fuel" mean in the last paragraph?
a drink taken during training

the strength left after exercise
food that supplies energy

qs.evidence: Young athletes who train in the morning need fuel before exercise, or they lose strength in the second half.
qs.answer: food that supplies energy
qs.why: Yang dibutuhin sebelum olahraga itu makanan sebagai sumber tenaga.
qs.whyOthersFail: Minuman saat latihan nggak pernah disebut. Obat dengan makanan itu kelompok kedua yang lain. Tenaga yang tersisa justru akibat kalau “fuel” nggak ada, bukan arti katanya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Research on adults has produced no single rule about breakfast."

qs.answer: True

qs.whyOthersFail: “False” nggak bisa karena nggak ada yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena hasil studinya ditulis.

title: The Gamelan in the Storeroom
text:
When Sari joined the school in Year 10, the gamelan instruments lay under a plastic sheet in the storeroom. Nobody had performed on them for four years, and two of the bronze keys remained missing. The music teacher had left, and the timetable offered guitar instead.

Sari asked for the key to the room and cleaned one instrument every Friday. Her father, a metal worker, made two replacement keys from an old pipe. In March she persuaded several classmates to try a simple piece. They practised behind the hall, where nobody could hear the mistakes.

The group played at the Independence Day assembly in August. The sound remained rough, and one boy started too early. Even so, three teachers asked whether their classes could join. The school has now hired a teacher for Tuesday afternoons, and the storeroom holds tables again, not instruments.
qs: Overall, what does this story show about the gamelan instruments?
A father made two keys from an old pipe
A school hired a music teacher for Tuesdays
One pupil's patience revived a silent set
A group played at the August assembly

qs.evidence: The school has now hired a teacher for Tuesday afternoons, and the storeroom holds tables again, not instruments.
qs.answer: One pupil's patience revived a silent set
qs.why: Gara-gara ketekunan satu murid, alat yang nganggur balik dipakai dan sekolah nyewa guru.

title: Email: Your Booking at the Guest House
text:
Dear Ms Wulan, thank you for your booking for four nights in July. We have reserved two rooms on the upper floor, both with a fan and a private bathroom. Breakfast is served between six and nine in the courtyard.

Two details require your attention. The road to the guest house is steep, and a wide vehicle cannot reach the gate. Most guests park beside the mosque and walk the last two hundred metres. Our driver can carry your luggage if you inform us of your arrival time.

The village celebrates its harvest festival during your stay. The music continues until late, and the upper rooms face the square. If you prefer a quiet night, we can transfer you to the back of the building. Those rooms have no view of the valley. Please confirm within three days, because the guest house remains full that week. Warm wishes, Ibu Ratih.

To confirm the booking and raise two matters

title: The Best Hour to Visit a Museum
text:
Museums are busiest between eleven and two, when tour groups and school parties arrive together. Guides recognize this pattern, so they plan their own visits around it. Two windows remain comparatively calm: the first hour after opening and the last ninety minutes before the doors close.

An early visit has clear advantages. The light in the halls is fresh, the staff have time for questions, and the temporary exhibition is still empty. The disadvantage is simple: cafés and shops inside the building may not be open yet.

A late visit suits people who dislike rushing. Attendants begin to close the far rooms about thirty minutes before the end. A late visitor should therefore walk to the most distant gallery first. Whichever hour you select, purchase the ticket online. The queue at the desk is often longer than the queue at the door, and a printed ticket costs the same.
qs: Overall, what advice does this text give about visiting a museum?
Why guides plan their visits so carefully
Choosing a calmer time to visit a museum
How attendants close the far rooms early
Why online tickets cost the same as printed ones

qs.evidence: Two windows remain comparatively calm: the first hour after opening and the last ninety minutes before the doors close.
qs.answer: Choosing a calmer time to visit a museum
qs.why: Isinya soal milih jam yang lebih lengang buat datang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Kebiasaan pemandu, penutupan ruang jauh, dan harga tiket daring semuanya rincian pendukung. Pokok artikelnya memilih jam berkunjung yang lebih lengang.

qs: Overall, what is the drawback of an early visit?
The halls may look darker in the early light
You may wait a while for a hot drink
The staff may have little time for questions
The temporary exhibition is already crowded

qs.evidence: The disadvantage is simple: cafés and shops inside the building may not be open yet.
qs.answer: You may wait a while for a hot drink

qs.whyOthersFail: Teks bilang cahaya pagi di ruang pamer justru segar. Petugas pagi malah punya waktu buat pertanyaan. Pameran sementara pun masih kosong di jam pertama.

qs: How should a late visitor plan a route through the museum?

buy a ticket at the desk by the door
ask an attendant when the far rooms close

qs.evidence: A late visitor should therefore walk to the most distant gallery first.
qs.answer: walk to the furthest gallery before the others
qs.why: Ruang terjauh ditutup lebih dulu, jadi ke sana dulu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nyaranin beli tiket daring, bukan di loket. Bertanya ke penjaga nggak pernah disaranin; jam tutup ruang jauh udah ditulis. Pameran sementara disebut buat pengunjung pagi.

qs: Why does the writer recommend buying online?
Because an online ticket costs a little less
Because the desk may shut at two in the afternoon
Because tour groups often book the calm hours first
Because the desk queue usually moves more slowly

qs.evidence: The queue at the desk is often longer than the queue at the door, and a printed ticket costs the same.
qs.answer: Because the desk queue usually moves more slowly

qs.whyOthersFail: Teks tegas bilang harganya sama, bukan lebih murah. Jam tutup loket nggak pernah disebut. Kelompok wisata datang jam sibuk, dan pemesanan mereka nggak dibahas.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Guides arrange their own visits to avoid the crowded hours."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Guides arrange their own visits to avoid the crowded hours.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Guides recognize this pattern, so they plan their own visits around it.
qs.why: “Plan their visits around it” artinya mereka ngatur jadwal biar nggak kena jam padat.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” nggak bisa karena nggak ada bagian yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena kebiasaan pemandu ditulis.

title: Report: Year 9 Trip to the Mangrove Park
text:
Ninety Year 9 pupils spent Saturday at the mangrove park on the coast. The buses left at half past six and returned at four. Each group of ten worked with a ranger, who showed them how the roots hold the mud in place.

The main activity was measurement. Pupils counted young trees inside squares of two metres, and they recorded the numbers on waterproof cards. The park keeps these cards, because the same squares are checked every year. Our figures showed thirty-one young trees in the wettest square and only nine in the driest.

Two problems appeared. Three pupils forgot boots and had to stay on the walkway, and the tide arrived earlier than the printed schedule promised. Next year the teachers will confirm the tide table a week in advance. The park has invited the school to return in the dry season, when the ranger can show the crab nests.

How mangrove roots hold mud and why the park charges
The tide table and the boots that three pupils forgot
A field trip, its findings and its problems

qs.answer: A field trip, its findings and its problems

title: Why Cover Versions Sell
text:
Every talent show produces the same complaint: young singers only copy famous songs. The habit looks lazy, but it has a good reason. An audience relaxes when it recognizes a tune, so a familiar song gives the singer a friendly start.

Musicians also learn from the work. Rewriting a song for two guitars teaches more about how music is built than a theory lesson does. When a singer moves a song from a major key to a minor one, the words gain a different weight. The class can hear the change at once.

The risk is comfort. A performer who repeats safe songs for two years builds no personal voice. The audience remembers the original singer instead. Teachers therefore suggest a balance: one cover, one original piece, and honest feedback after each performance. The second song is always harder to write, but it belongs to the writer.
qs: Overall, what point does this text make about singing cover versions?
An audience relaxes, and a familiar tune wins the prize
Covers teach a lot, but they can also trap a singer
Teachers ask for feedback, and pupils write it down
A minor key adds weight, and the class prefers it

qs.whyOthersFail: Penonton memang santai, tapi soal menang lomba nggak pernah ditulis. Masukan jujur diberikan guru, dan nggak disebut dicatat murid. Nada minor mengubah bobot lirik, tapi selera kelas nggak dibahas.

qs.whyOthersFail: Teks nggak bilang penonton mengawasi perubahan aransemen. Penyanyi asli memang teringat, tapi itu risiko jangka panjang, bukan reaksi saat lagunya dikenali. Ikut menyanyi juga nggak pernah disebut.

qs.whyOthersFail: Memilih nada buat suara nggak disebut sebagai pelajarannya. Masukan jujur datang dari guru sesudah penampilan. Selera penonton dibahas di paragraf pertama, bukan hasil menyusun ulang lagu.

title: Announcement: Tree Planting on the River Bank
text:
The district office will plant six hundred trees along the river bank on the last Sunday of the month. Volunteers from every school are invited, and the work starts at half past six, before the heat.

Please examine the practical arrangements. Wear long trousers and closed shoes, because the mud hides sharp shells. Bring a bottle of water; the office will provide gloves and a simple lunch. Anyone under fifteen must attend with an adult. Groups will be registered at the gate beside the bridge.

The young trees were selected for wet ground, so please follow the marks left by the forest staff. Trees planted too close to the water wash away in the first storm. After the planting, three volunteers from each school will assist with the monthly check of the young trees. Sign the list in your school office within a week, because the gloves must be counted in advance.

author: District office
setting: a river bank in the district

title: Give Year Eleven a Real Careers Hour
text:
Every Friday afternoon our school runs a careers hour that almost nobody treats seriously. Pupils are handed a leaflet, instructed to read it at home, and then sent away. Meanwhile the questions that worry them most are never addressed, and no member of staff appears responsible. How do you prepare a first application for a temporary post? What obligations does a training contract actually involve? I believe the school is wasting a decent idea by refusing to organize it properly.
The failure is not the pupils' fault. Last term the student council surveyed 210 learners about the purpose of the hour; only 19 requested additional leaflets. Nearly three quarters asked to meet people who had recently entered paid employment. Surely a gap of that scale reveals something about our priorities. Having read the results, our head of year admitted that the current plan was designed for teachers, not for the people sitting in the room.
A better version would demand very little money and no additional staff. Invite three former pupils each month, grant them ten minutes each, and permit students to ask anything. Replace the leaflet with a brief practical session on written applications. If the school attempted this for one term, I am confident that attendance would rise on its own. A careers hour that answers genuine questions is worth far more than a tidy folder nobody opens.
