qs: What is the writer mainly trying to do in this article?
urge pupils to arrange their own careers sessions instead
urge the school to rebuild the careers hour properly
urge staff to hand out the leaflet earlier each week
urge the council to pay for extra careers staff

qs.evidence: I believe the school is wasting a decent idea by refusing to organize it properly.
qs.answer: urge the school to rebuild the careers hour properly
qs.why: Penulis nulis “I believe the school is wasting a decent idea by refusing to organize it properly”, jadi dorongannya ke sekolah supaya jam itu disusun ulang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiga-tiganya usul yang wajar buat sekolah mana pun, tapi teks memblokir semuanya: “The failure is not the pupils' fault” bikin tugas itu nggak dilempar ke murid; penulis mau leaflet-nya diganti (“Replace the leaflet with a brief practical session”), bukan dibagikan lebih awal; dan “would demand very little money and no additional staff” nutup usul minta dana staf tambahan ke dinas.

qs: Which supporting detail from the student council survey strengthens the case for rebuilding the careers hour?
nearly three quarters of those asked wanted to meet people newly in work
most of the 210 learners asked for more leaflets to read at home
only nineteen learners wanted the hour moved to a Friday morning
the head of year said the present plan had been designed for pupils

qs.evidence: Nearly three quarters asked to meet people who had recently entered paid employment.
qs.answer: nearly three quarters of those asked wanted to meet people newly in work
qs.why: Detail pendukungnya angka survei: hampir tiga per empat dari 210 pelajar minta bertemu orang yang baru masuk dunia kerja, persis isi jam yang diusulkan penulis.
qs.whyOthersFail: Leaflet tambahan cuma diminta 19 dari 210 pelajar, jadi bukan permintaan mayoritas. Angka 19 itu soal leaflet, bukan soal memindahkan jam ke Jumat pagi — pemindahan jadwal nggak pernah disurvei. Dan kepala tingkat mengakui rencana itu disusun “for teachers, not for the people sitting in the room”, kebalikan opsi terakhir.

qs: Which detail best supports the claim that the present plan suits staff rather than students?
no member of staff appears responsible for the hour
pupils are told to read the leaflet at home
the head of year agreed the plan favoured staff
only nineteen learners asked for additional leaflets

qs.evidence: Having read the results, our head of year admitted that the current plan was designed for teachers, not for the people sitting in the room.
qs.answer: the head of year agreed the plan favoured staff
qs.why: Pengakuan “the current plan was designed for teachers, not for the people sitting in the room” langsung nyatain rencananya dibikin buat guru, jadi itu dukungan paling tepat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya beneran ada di teks dan sama-sama kedengaran seperti bukti, tapi nggak nyentuh klaimnya: “no member of staff appears responsible” nunjukin nggak ada yang ngurus, bukan bahwa jamnya dirancang buat guru; “instructed to read it at home” cuma nunjukin sesinya dangkal; dan “only 19 requested additional leaflets” ngukur selera murid, bukan buat siapa rencananya disusun.

qs: What does the writer suggest about attendance at the careers hour?
attendance would probably hold up if the leaflet improved
attendance would probably rise once real questions were answered
attendance would probably need a register to be enforced
attendance would probably recover if alumni visited every week

qs.evidence: If the school attempted this for one term, I am confident that attendance would rise on its own.
qs.answer: attendance would probably rise once real questions were answered
qs.why: Penulis bilang “If the school attempted this for one term, I am confident that attendance would rise on its own”, dan yang dia usulkan adalah sesi yang jawab pertanyaan sungguhan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Semuanya cara masuk akal buat naikin kehadiran, tapi teks nutup tiga di antaranya: leaflet-nya mau diganti, bukan diperbaiki (“Replace the leaflet”); “would rise on its own” justru nolak perlunya paksaan atau absensi; dan usulnya “Invite three former pupils each month”, bukan alumni tiap minggu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Only a small number of those asked wanted extra leaflets."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Only a small number of those asked wanted extra leaflets.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Last term the student council surveyed 210 learners about the purpose of the hour; only 19 requested additional leaflets.
qs.why: Teks nyebut cuma 19 dari 210 pelajar yang minta leaflet tambahan, jadi “a small number” itu parafrasa angka yang sama.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” nggak jalan karena teks nggak ngebalik jumlahnya; “Not stated” juga salah karena angkanya ditulis jelas.

author: a Year Eleven form teacher
setting: a secondary school in a mid-sized town

title: What Happened When One Lane Became a Bus Lane
text:
For six months a research team from a city college observed one crowded road in an urban district of Bandung. The council had converted one of its three lanes into a bus lane, and local drivers protested immediately. The team wanted to establish what that decision had actually caused. They counted vehicles, measured journey times, and interviewed 340 residents at both ends of the route.
The results were mixed but reasonably clear. Buses arrived on time far more often, and the average bus journey fell from 31 minutes to 22. Private cars did lose road space, yet car journeys grew longer by only two minutes, because fewer people were driving. About one in nine former drivers had switched to the bus service by the final month. The researchers argue that the delay drivers feared was largely caused by their own numbers, not by the missing lane.
The report warns against copying the scheme without careful thought. Where no bus operates every few minutes, a reserved lane simply stands empty and public patience disappears. The team therefore recommends three conditions: a frequent service, clear signs, and a review after one year. Their conclusion is cautious but firm. Granting space to the vehicle that carries the largest number of people remains the cheapest method of moving a crowded street.
qs: Taken together, what case does this report build for reserving a lane?
a reserved lane helps most where few cars use the road
a reserved lane moves the delay from buses onto private cars
a reserved lane earns public patience once its signs are clear
a reserved lane cuts delay where buses arrive every few minutes

qs.evidence: The team therefore recommends three conditions: a frequent service, clear signs, and a review after one year.
qs.answer: a reserved lane cuts delay where buses arrive every few minutes
qs.why: Tiga syarat penutup laporan — “a frequent service, clear signs, and a review after one year” — bikin intinya: lajur bus ngurangin keterlambatan asal busnya sering.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya bacaan yang wajar buat studi lalu lintas, tapi teks ngeblok satu-satu: jalannya justru “one crowded road”, jadi bukan jalan yang sepi mobil; “car journeys grew longer by only two minutes” nolak gagasan keterlambatan dipindah ke mobil; dan rambu jelas cuma satu dari tiga syarat, sementara “Where no bus operates every few minutes, a reserved lane simply stands empty” naruh frekuensi bus sebagai penentunya.

qs: Taken together, what do the report's timings show about the average bus journey after the change?
roughly thirty-one minutes
about twenty-eight minutes
about twenty-two minutes
roughly nineteen minutes

qs.evidence: Buses arrived on time far more often, and the average bus journey fell from 31 minutes to 22.
qs.answer: about twenty-two minutes
qs.why: Teks nyebut rata-rata perjalanan bus turun dari 31 menit jadi 22 menit setelah jalur dibikin.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiga puluh satu menit adalah angka sebelum lajur dibuka, bukan sesudah; dan dua puluh delapan serta sembilan belas menit nggak muncul di laporan — penurunannya dari 31 ke 22 menit.

qs: How did car journeys compare with bus journeys once the lane opened?
cars lost a couple of minutes while buses saved about four
cars lost about nine minutes while buses saved a couple
cars kept their old times while buses saved about nine minutes
cars lost a couple of minutes while buses saved about nine

qs.evidence: Private cars did lose road space, yet car journeys grew longer by only two minutes, because fewer people were driving.
qs.answer: cars lost a couple of minutes while buses saved about nine
qs.why: Mobil cuma nambah dua menit sementara bus turun dari 31 ke 22 menit, jadi kerugian mobil kecil dan hematan bus sembilan menit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya pola hasil yang masuk akal buat lajur bus, tapi angka teksnya beda: “fell from 31 minutes to 22” bikin hematan bus sembilan menit, bukan empat dan bukan cuma dua; dan “car journeys grew longer by only two minutes” nunjukin waktu mobil tetap berubah, jadi bukan sama seperti dulu.

qs: Which conclusion about the delay drivers feared do the team's counts and journey times best support?
much of the delay came from the number of cars themselves
the delay was created mainly by the lane that was taken away
the delay continued because drivers ignored the new signs
the delay grew because buses kept stopping in mixed traffic

qs.evidence: The researchers argue that the delay drivers feared was largely caused by their own numbers, not by the missing lane.
qs.answer: much of the delay came from the number of cars themselves
qs.why: Bukti di teks menuntun ke satu simpulan: waktu tempuh mobil cuma naik dua menit “because fewer people were driving”, dan peneliti nyimpulin keterlambatan yang ditakuti pengemudi “was largely caused by their own numbers, not by the missing lane”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya tuduhan yang wajar di kota mana pun, tapi teks nutup semuanya. Frasa “not by the missing lane” nolak lajur yang dihapus sebagai sebab. Rambu cuma muncul sebagai syarat keberhasilan (“clear signs”), bukan sebagai sesuatu yang diabaikan pengemudi. Dan bus justru dapat lajur sendiri, jadi berhenti di lalu lintas campur nggak pernah diukur.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "By the last month, most former car drivers had moved to the bus."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: By the last month, most former car drivers had moved to the bus.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: About one in nine former drivers had switched to the bus service by the final month.
qs.why: Teks bilang kira-kira satu dari sembilan pengemudi lama yang pindah ke bus, jadi klaim “most” ngebalik jumlahnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena satu per sembilan jauh dari mayoritas; “Not stated” nggak bisa dipakai karena angka perpindahannya ada di teks.

author: a transport reporter
setting: a three-lane road in an urban district of Bandung

title: New Phone or Second-hand? Two Honest Options
text:
Anyone replacing a phone this year encounters the same choice: pay the full price for a new model, or purchase a used one from a repair shop. Both routes now include a guarantee, so the traditional warning about risk no longer settles the matter. What separates them is the kind of cost you are willing to accept.
A new phone wins on certainty and predictability. You obtain an unmarked screen, a fresh battery, and software updates for perhaps five years. The price, however, is roughly double the amount a two-year-old repaired handset costs. A used phone wins on value and on waste. Its battery may already have lost a fifth of its original capacity, and the case will display small marks. In exchange, buyers keep a functioning device out of the bin and save enough for a year of travel.
Retailers naturally emphasize whichever margin favours them. So which should you select? If you intend to keep a phone until it dies, the new model probably repays its price in additional years of updates. If you change devices frequently, or you mainly want a camera and messages, the second-hand route is the sensible one. My own view is that most shoppers overestimate how much newness they require. The honest question is not which phone is better, but how long you intend to keep it.
qs: What is the writer's main purpose in this article?
to help each kind of buyer match a route to the guarantee
to show that guarantees have made the two routes equal
to warn buyers that retailers hide the real cost gap
to help each kind of buyer match a route to their habits

qs.evidence: What separates them is the kind of cost you are willing to accept.
qs.answer: to help each kind of buyer match a route to their habits
qs.why: Teks bilang “What separates them is the kind of cost you are willing to accept”, lalu tiap paragraf nunjuk pembeli mana yang cocok ke jalur mana.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya niat yang masuk akal buat artikel belanja, tapi teks ngeblok: “Both routes now include a guarantee” bikin garansi nggak bisa jadi pembeda antar-pembeli maupun bukti kedua jalur setara; dan penjual cuma disebut sekali (“emphasize whichever margin favours them”), bukan jadi sasaran artikel.

qs: Taken together, what do the article's warnings show about the battery of a used phone?
it is usually replaced before the phone is resold
it tends to outlast the battery of a new handset
some of its original power may have gone already
it is the one part left outside the guarantee

qs.evidence: Its battery may already have lost a fifth of its original capacity, and the case will display small marks.
qs.answer: some of its original power may have gone already
qs.why: Teks nyebut baterainya mungkin udah kehilangan seperlima kapasitas aslinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nggak ada kalimat soal baterai diganti sebelum dijual lagi; dayanya juga digambarkan berkurang, jadi mustahil lebih tahan dari baterai baru; dan garansi di teks berlaku buat kedua jalur tanpa pengecualian bagian baterai.

qs: How do the two options compare on price?
the used route saves roughly a fifth of the new price
the new route costs roughly twice the repaired handset's price
the new route costs roughly twice its price two years ago
the used route costs roughly the same once repairs are added

qs.evidence: The price, however, is roughly double the amount a two-year-old repaired handset costs.
qs.answer: the new route costs roughly twice the repaired handset's price
qs.why: Harga ponsel baru disebut “roughly double the amount a two-year-old repaired handset costs”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya selisih harga yang wajar di pasar ponsel, tapi angka teksnya lain: “roughly double” jauh lebih besar dari seperlima, dan “a fifth” di teks itu kapasitas baterai yang hilang; perbandingannya juga sama handset bekas berumur dua tahun, bukan sama harga model itu dua tahun lalu; dan kalau harganya sama, seluruh alinea biaya nggak masuk akal.

qs: Which statement best restates the writer's advice in the last paragraph?
how long you plan to keep the phone should settle the choice
how much the newest model now costs should settle the choice
how well the camera and messages work should settle the choice
how many years of updates you get should settle the choice

qs.evidence: The honest question is not which phone is better, but how long you intend to keep it.
qs.answer: how long you plan to keep the phone should settle the choice
qs.why: Kalimat penutup nyebut “The honest question is not which phone is better, but how long you intend to keep it”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya patokan yang benar-benar dipakai pembeli, tapi teks naruhnya di bawah lamanya pemakaian: harga cuma pembanding (“roughly double”), kamera dan pesan cuma contoh buat satu tipe pembeli (“mainly want a camera and messages”), dan lima tahun update disebut sebagai imbalan yang balik modal “If you intend to keep a phone until it dies” — jadi tetap lamanya pemakaian yang mutusin.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "A repaired handset comes with a two-year guarantee from the shop."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: A repaired handset comes with a two-year guarantee from the shop.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Both routes now include a guarantee, so the traditional warning about risk no longer settles the matter.
qs.why: Teks cuma nyebut kedua jalur sekarang datang dengan guarantee, tanpa pernah nyebut garansinya berlaku berapa lama, jadi angka dua tahun nggak bisa kamu pastiin dari teks.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena durasi garansi nggak pernah ditulis; “False” juga salah karena teks nggak nyatain garansinya lebih pendek atau lebih panjang — soal lamanya dia memang diam.

author: a consumer columnist
setting: a consumer column about phone shopping

title: A Notes App That Asks for Almost Nothing
text:
Quiet Notes is a free writing app that has become popular in schools, and its selling point is what it refuses to do. It requests no contact list, no location, and no advertising identifier. On first opening it displays a single screen listing every permission it will ever require. Honesty of that kind is rare enough to deserve a review.
As a notebook the app is competent rather than brilliant. Typing is quick, folders are simple to construct, and the search box locates a word across hundreds of pages in a second. Yet the design feels plain beside its commercial rivals, and there is no drawing tool at all. Notes are stored on the device itself and copied to one rented server abroad. The developers also publish an annual report on requests received from officials. Export options are limited to plain text and a single archive.
Where the app genuinely wins is in the small print. Its privacy notice extends to 600 words and is entirely free of the usual fog. Where it loses is in the features that many pupils actually want. If you need shared editing or handwriting, look elsewhere; if you want a place to think that does not study you, install it today. Four marks out of five, with one withheld for the missing drawing tool.
qs: Taken together, what verdict does this review reach about the notes app?
notes stay on the device but travel to one rented server abroad
the app offers a plain feature list but unusual honesty
the developers publish a yearly report but limit export to two forms
the app wins on speed rather than on what it promises

qs.evidence: Where the app genuinely wins is in the small print.
qs.answer: the app offers a plain feature list but unusual honesty
qs.why: Resensinya nyimpulin “Where the app genuinely wins is in the small print” sambil ngakui fiturnya “competent rather than brilliant”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh adalah klaim yang betul-betul ada di paragraf kedua ulasan ini, tetapi masing-masing keterangan sampingan, bukan penilaian pokoknya. Penyimpanan di perangkat dan satu server sewaan hanyalah rincian teknis di tengah daftar fitur. Laporan tahunan tentang permintaan pejabat serta ekspor yang terbatas pada dua bentuk adalah dua rincian yang benar tetapi bukan pertimbangan yang ditimbang ulasan ini. Kecepatan kotak pencarian termasuk dalam bagian yang dinilai "competent rather than brilliant". Penekanannya disebut sendiri oleh penulis: "Where the app genuinely wins is in the small print" berbanding "the design feels plain beside its commercial rivals". Opsi terakhir memang berbentuk rangkuman, tetapi salah arah: kecepatan justru dinilai "competent rather than brilliant", sedangkan janji kecillah yang dipuji.

qs: Taken together, what does the review say the app shows a user on first opening?
a short note about the server it rents abroad
a note on where the notes are stored
its yearly report on requests from officials
a screen naming the permissions it will request

qs.evidence: On first opening it displays a single screen listing every permission it will ever require.
qs.answer: a screen naming the permissions it will request
qs.why: Saat pertama dibuka, aplikasinya nampilin satu layar yang mendaftar semua izin yang akan pernah dia minta.
qs.whyOthersFail: Server sewaan di luar negeri dan laporan tahunan memang ada, tapi keduanya dibahas belakangan, bukan di layar pertama; tempat penyimpanan catatan juga nggak ditampilkan saat pertama dibuka — yang muncul satu layar berisi semua izin yang akan diminta.

qs: Which detail best supports the reviewer's praise for the small print?
it asks for no contact list, location, or advertising identifier
its terms fill only 600 words of plain, readable English
it publishes a yearly report on requests made by officials
it names every permission on one screen at first opening

qs.evidence: Its privacy notice extends to 600 words and is entirely free of the usual fog.
qs.answer: its terms fill only 600 words of plain, readable English
qs.why: Pujian buat “small print” nunjuk notis privasinya sendiri: “extends to 600 words and is entirely free of the usual fog”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya benar-benar ada di teks dan sama-sama nunjukin aplikasinya terbuka, tapi bukan soal syarat tertulisnya: izin yang nggak diminta dan “a single screen listing every permission” itu perilaku aplikasi, dan laporan tahunan soal permintaan pejabat itu praktik perusahaan — cuma notis 600 kata yang bicara soal small print.

qs: What can be inferred about pupils who like to sketch their notes?
they will probably use the archive export to move their sketches
they will probably find the plain design suits sketching well
they will probably wait for the drawing tool to be added
they will probably have to look for another app instead

qs.evidence: Yet the design feels plain beside its commercial rivals, and there is no drawing tool at all.
qs.answer: they will probably have to look for another app instead
qs.why: Teks nyebut “there is no drawing tool at all” dan nyuruh “if you need shared editing or handwriting, look elsewhere”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya jalan keluar yang wajar buat pengguna, tapi teksnya nutup: ekspornya cuma “plain text and a single archive”, jadi nggak nampung gambar; desain polos disebut kelemahan (“feels plain beside its commercial rivals”), bukan bantuan buat nyoret; dan nggak ada janji alat gambar bakal datang — satu nilai malah ditahan gara-gara alat itu nggak ada.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The app keeps a copy of notes on a server outside the country."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The app keeps a copy of notes on a server outside the country.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Notes are stored on the device itself and copied to one rented server abroad.
qs.why: “abroad” di teks sama artinya sama “outside the country”, dan teks jelas nyebut salinan catatan disimpan di server sewaan itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” salah karena nggak ada proposisi yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena penyimpanan di server luar disebut langsung.

author: a technology reviewer
setting: a technology review page

title: Letter: Please Review the Evening Pool Timetable
text:
Dear Ms Halim, I am writing on behalf of the school swimming club. Our purpose is to request a review of the evening timetable, which was altered at the start of this term. Our club trains on four evenings weekly and has done so for eleven years. We recognize that demand for lanes is considerable and that the centre must balance competing groups. We accept that the centre must serve every category of user, and we submit our request in that spirit.
The difficulty is straightforward. Club training now commences at nine o'clock, an hour later than previously, and concludes at half past ten. Since the change, average attendance has declined from thirty-one swimmers to seventeen, and eight of our junior members have abandoned the sport. Parents state plainly that they refuse to collect a twelve-year-old at that hour. The new arrangement therefore protects the pool's evening income while quietly closing the club to children. The consequence is a session that excludes precisely the members who benefit most from regular exercise. Two independent coaches have described the situation as unsustainable for a junior programme.
We would prefer to propose a compromise rather than a complaint. Two lanes from eight until nine would enable our junior squad to train, while the remaining lanes remain available to the public. If the centre prefers, we are willing to transfer one session to weekend mornings and to pay the usual lane fee. Such a compromise would protect your evening income while restoring access for junior swimmers. I should be grateful for an opportunity to discuss this before the month concludes. Yours sincerely, Dita Rahman, club secretary.
qs: Why was this letter written?
to ask the centre to drop the evening fee for juniors
to ask the centre for an earlier hour for the junior squad
to ask the centre to reserve every lane for club training
to ask the centre to move all club sessions to weekends

qs.evidence: We would prefer to propose a compromise rather than a complaint.
qs.answer: to ask the centre for an earlier hour for the junior squad
qs.why: Surat nawarin “Two lanes from eight until nine would enable our junior squad to train”, jadi yang diminta jam yang lebih awal buat regu junior.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya permintaan yang masuk akal dari sebuah klub, tapi suratnya ngeblok: klub nyatain “willing to transfer one session to weekend mornings and to pay the usual lane fee”, jadi biaya nggak diminta dihapus dan yang dipindah cuma satu sesi; dan “the remaining lanes remain available to the public” nolak minta semua lajur.

qs: Taken together, what do the club's attendance figures show about the new timetable?
it stayed close to thirty-one swimmers a night
it fell only among the club's adult members
it fell by about a fifth of the earlier figure
it fell to roughly half the earlier figure

qs.evidence: Since the change, average attendance has declined from thirty-one swimmers to seventeen, and eight of our junior members have abandoned the sport.
qs.answer: it fell to roughly half the earlier figure
qs.why: Kehadiran rata-rata turun dari 31 perenang jadi 17, jadi kira-kira separuh dari angka sebelumnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Tiga puluh satu itu angka sebelum perubahan, bukan sesudahnya; penurunannya bukan cuma di anggota dewasa karena delapan anggota junior berhenti; dan turunnya dari 31 ke 17 jauh lebih dalam daripada seperlima.

qs: Which point best supports the claim that the new slot shuts children out?
average attendance has fallen from thirty-one swimmers to seventeen
two independent coaches call the timetable unsustainable
the club has trained four evenings a week for eleven years
families will not fetch a child of twelve so late

qs.evidence: Parents state plainly that they refuse to collect a twelve-year-old at that hour.
qs.answer: families will not fetch a child of twelve so late
qs.why: Kalimat “Parents state plainly that they refuse to collect a twelve-year-old at that hour” nunjukin persisnya kenapa slot baru nutup pintu buat anak-anak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya ada di surat dan kedengaran mendukung, tapi nggak nyentuh anaknya: angka “from thirty-one swimmers to seventeen” ngitung semua anggota, bukan cuma junior; penilaian “unsustainable for a junior programme” itu pendapat pelatih tanpa nyebut sebabnya; dan latihan sebelas tahun cuma nunjukin klubnya lama, bukan bahwa anak-anak kekunci di luar.

qs: What does the letter suggest about the club's attitude to the centre?
the club wants an outcome that protects both sides' interests
the club expects the centre to reject any offer it makes
the club believes the centre has failed its adult members too
the club is ready to train elsewhere if the answer is no

qs.evidence: Two lanes from eight until nine would enable our junior squad to train, while the remaining lanes remain available to the public.
qs.answer: the club wants an outcome that protects both sides' interests
qs.why: Usulan “Two lanes from eight until nine ... while the remaining lanes remain available to the public” nunjukin klub nyari jalan yang aman buat dua pihak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya sikap yang biasa muncul di surat sengketa jadwal, tapi teks ngeblok: klub nulis “We would prefer to propose a compromise rather than a complaint” dan minta ketemu, jadi dia nggak nunggu penolakan; keluhannya khusus junior (“closing the club to children”), bukan anggota dewasa; dan nggak ada satu kalimat pun soal pindah kolam.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Club training now finishes at half past nine each night."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Club training now finishes at half past nine each night.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Club training now commences at nine o'clock, an hour later than previously, and concludes at half past ten.
qs.why: Setengah sepuluh itu jam mulai plus setengah jam, padahal teks nyebut latihan baru selesai setengah sebelas.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena waktunya digeser satu jam; “Not stated” salah karena jam selesai latihan ditulis jelas.

topic: a swimming club and pool hours
author: the club secretary
setting: a letter to the manager of a leisure centre

title: Yes, the Cycle Lane Deserves That Road Space
text:
Whenever a city paints a cycle lane, the same objection returns: why grant a third of the road to a handful of riders? It sounds reasonable, and it is wrong. The people who raise it are counting bicycles at eight in the morning on a street that has been unsafe for twenty years. Demand does not appear before the lane; it appears afterwards.
Consider the two claims side by side. Opponents insist that lanes remove space from vehicles which carry more passengers. Supporters answer that a protected lane moves up to five times as many people each hour as a queue of cars. Both sides can quote figures, yet only one of them has to explain why parents refuse to let their children ride. I have cycled to work in this district for nine years, and the reason most of my neighbours remain in their cars is fear rather than comfort.
None of this makes every lane sensible. A lane that stops at a busy roundabout, or one painted between parked cars and moving buses, is worse than nothing. What we should demand is a network joining schools, markets, and stations without a single frightening gap. Until then, complaining about empty lanes resembles blaming an unfinished bridge for the river. A network of that kind demands political courage and steady investment. Construct the network properly and the riders will arrive.
qs: Taken together, what argument does this column build about empty cycle lanes?
the case for lanes rests on how many people they move
a lane ending at a roundabout is worse than having none at all
fear rather than comfort keeps the writer's neighbours in their cars
empty lanes show only that the network is still unfinished

qs.evidence: Until then, complaining about empty lanes resembles blaming an unfinished bridge for the river.
qs.answer: empty lanes show only that the network is still unfinished
qs.why: Penulis nutup argumennya sama perumpamaan “complaining about empty lanes resembles blaming an unfinished bridge for the river”, jadi jalur yang kelihatan kosong cuma nandain jaringannya belum nyambung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh adalah klaim nyata dari paragraf lain kolom ini, tetapi tak satu pun menjadi hujah utamanya. Angka lima kali lipat adalah jawaban pihak pendukung yang dikutip penulis untuk menunjukkan kedua kubu punya angka. Lajur yang berhenti di bundaran muncul sebagai kelonggaran, "None of this makes every lane sensible". Rasa takut para tetangga adalah bukti pendukung dari pengalaman penulis. Penekanannya ada pada "Until then, complaining about empty lanes resembles blaming an unfinished bridge for the river". Opsi pertama juga berbentuk rangkuman, tetapi angka kapasitas itu dibawa penulis sebagai jawaban pihak pendukung, bukan sebagai tumpuan hujahnya sendiri.

qs: Which figure quoted by supporters props up the writer's case for giving a lane the road space?
a protected lane moves up to five times as many people an hour as a car queue
counts of bicycles at eight in the morning have risen over twenty years
a lane painted between parked cars and buses still beats having none
the writer's neighbours stay in their cars because cycling is uncomfortable

qs.evidence: Supporters answer that a protected lane moves up to five times as many people each hour as a queue of cars.
qs.answer: a protected lane moves up to five times as many people an hour as a car queue
qs.why: Angka pendukung yang dipakai penulis: jalur terlindung mengangkut sampai lima kali lebih banyak orang per jam dibanding antrean mobil, jadi ruang jalan itu bukan buat “a handful of riders”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Hitungan sepeda jam delapan pagi adalah cara pihak penentang, dan teks nggak pernah bilang hitungan itu naik — yang disebut naik dua puluh tahun adalah lamanya jalan itu nggak aman. Jalur di antara mobil parkir dan bus disebut “worse than nothing”, jadi bukan pendukung. Dan alasan tetangga tetap di mobil adalah “fear rather than comfort”.

qs: How does the writer contrast the two sides of the argument?
only supporters count riders at a fair hour of day
only one side has to answer why families stay afraid
only opponents use figures, while supporters use experience
only riders who already feel safe appear in either count

qs.evidence: Both sides can quote figures, yet only one of them has to explain why parents refuse to let their children ride.
qs.answer: only one side has to answer why families stay afraid
qs.why: Teks bilang “Both sides can quote figures, yet only one of them has to explain why parents refuse to let their children ride”, jadi bebannya nggak seimbang cuma di soal rasa takut.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya kedengaran masuk akal buat adu argumen dengan angka, tapi teks ngeblok: jam penghitungan cuma dipakai buat nyalahin penentang, bukan buat memuji kejujuran pendukung; “Both sides can quote figures” nolak gagasan cuma satu pihak pakai angka; dan teks nggak pernah nyebut siapa yang masuk hitungan, dia nyebut pesepeda baru muncul sesudah jalurnya ada.

qs: What does the writer imply about a lane that ends at a roundabout?
such a lane still helps riders who already feel confident
such a lane usually fills with riders within about a year
such a lane suits short trips between markets and stations
such a lane can leave riders worse off than before

qs.evidence: A lane that stops at a busy roundabout, or one painted between parked cars and moving buses, is worse than nothing.
qs.answer: such a lane can leave riders worse off than before
qs.why: Jalur yang berhenti di bundaran sibuk disebut “worse than nothing”, jadi pesepeda bisa lebih rugi daripada sebelum jalurnya ada.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya penilaian yang masuk akal buat jalur setengah jadi, tapi frasa “is worse than nothing” nutup semuanya: kalau lebih buruk daripada nggak ada, dia nggak bisa disebut tetap menolong yang percaya diri maupun cocok buat perjalanan pendek; dan penulis naruh datangnya pesepeda pada jaringan tanpa “a single frightening gap”, bukan pada jalur yang mentok di bundaran.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer says his neighbours avoid cycling mainly because they are afraid."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer says his neighbours avoid cycling mainly because they are afraid.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: I have cycled to work in this district for nine years, and the reason most of my neighbours remain in their cars is fear rather than comfort.
qs.why: Teks nyebut alasan tetangganya tetap di mobil itu rasa takut, bukan kenyamanan, jadi klaim ini parafrasa langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” salah karena alasannya nggak dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena alasan itu ditulis terang-terangan.

author: a daily cyclist and columnist
setting: an opinion column in a city newspaper

title: Late Training, Short Sleep, and Tired Mornings
text:
A study at a sports academy has traced a chain that many coaches suspected but few had measured properly. For ten weeks, 84 young footballers wore simple wrist monitors and recorded the hour at which they trained. Half the participants concluded practice at seven in the evening; the remainder finished at half past nine. Everything else in their weekly routine remained identical. Coaches at rival academies had assumed the difference was negligible.
The later group slept 47 minutes less on training nights. That loss did not result from a later bedtime alone. Body temperature and excitement after severe exercise kept the players alert for roughly half an hour once they lay down. In morning tests of reaction and short-term memory the late group scored about a tenth lower, and reported muscle pain that lasted a day longer. Recovery therefore occupied more of the following morning than the coaches had estimated. The chain therefore runs from the timetable to the sleep, and from the sleep to the following day.
The researchers are cautious about what follows. They observed one academy, one season, and one age group, so the figures should not be transferred elsewhere without checking. Even so, the direction of the effect was consistent across both squads. Their recommendation to clubs is modest and inexpensive. End evening sessions before eight where possible, reduce the lighting afterwards, and treat a late finish as part of the training load. Such adjustments require no equipment and no additional expense for the club.
qs: Taken together, what picture does this report give of late training and the next morning?
why heat and excitement keep players alert once they lie down
how much less the late squad slept on its training nights
how the hour of practice shapes the following morning
why one academy's figures should not be transferred elsewhere

qs.evidence: The chain therefore runs from the timetable to the sleep, and from the sleep to the following day.
qs.answer: how the hour of practice shapes the following morning
qs.why: Laporan nyebut rantainya lugas: “from the timetable to the sleep, and from the sleep to the following day”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh benar-benar dinyatakan dalam laporan ini, tetapi masing-masing satu mata rantai atau satu catatan kehati-hatian, bukan pokoknya. Suhu tubuh dan kegembiraan adalah penjelasan mengapa tidurnya berkurang, bukan temuannya. Selisih 47 menit adalah satu ukuran di dalam rantai itu. Peringatan agar angkanya nggak dipindahkan ke tempat lain adalah pembatasan cakupan. Penekanannya dinyatakan sendiri: "The chain therefore runs from the timetable to the sleep, and from the sleep to the following day".

qs: Taken together, what do the sleep records show about the later training group?
rather more than an hour
a little under fifty minutes
roughly a tenth of a night
about half an hour at the most

qs.evidence: The later group slept 47 minutes less on training nights.
qs.answer: a little under fifty minutes
qs.why: Kelompok yang latihan lebih malam tidur 47 menit lebih sedikit, jadi sedikit di bawah lima puluh menit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Lebih dari sejam melebihi angka teks; sepersepuluh malam adalah besarnya penurunan skor tes, bukan lama tidur yang hilang; dan setengah jam itu waktu yang dibutuhkan pemain buat tenang setelah latihan keras — kehilangan tidurnya 47 menit.

qs: Which finding best supports the claim that the lost sleep mattered the next day?
the later group slept forty-seven minutes less on training nights
excitement after hard exercise kept the players alert for a while
the direction of the effect held across both of the squads
the next day's tests of speed and recall came out worse

qs.evidence: In morning tests of reaction and short-term memory the late group scored about a tenth lower, and reported muscle pain that lasted a day longer.
qs.answer: the next day's tests of speed and recall came out worse
qs.why: Skor tes reaksi dan memori pagi turun sekitar sepersepuluh dan nyeri otot bertahan sehari lebih lama — itu akibat yang kebawa ke hari berikutnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya temuan asli studi ini, tapi nggak satu pun ngomongin hari berikutnya: 47 menit itu ukuran tidur yang hilang, bukan akibatnya; “kept the players alert for roughly half an hour” nerangin sebab hilangnya tidur; dan konsistensi arah efek antar dua regu ngomongin keandalan angka, bukan dampak paginya.

qs: Which statement best restates the researchers' warning about their findings?
the effect may well be weaker among older players elsewhere
the figures should carry over to most clubs without checking
one academy in one season cannot settle the matter alone
the effect appeared in only one of the two squads

qs.evidence: They observed one academy, one season, and one age group, so the figures should not be transferred elsewhere without checking.
qs.answer: one academy in one season cannot settle the matter alone
qs.why: Peneliti nekenin “They observed one academy, one season, and one age group, so the figures should not be transferred elsewhere without checking”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya kedengaran seperti kehati-hatian ilmiah yang biasa, tapi teksnya lain: peneliti nggak meramalkan efeknya melemah pada pemain lebih tua, mereka cuma bilang satu kelompok umur yang diamati; “should not be transferred elsewhere without checking” persis ngebalik opsi angka bisa dipakai di klub lain; dan “the direction of the effect was consistent across both squads” nolak klaim efeknya cuma di satu regu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Late training left the players hungrier than the early group."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Late training left the players hungrier than the early group.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Body temperature and excitement after severe exercise kept the players alert for roughly half an hour once they lay down.
qs.why: Teks ngukur tidur, suhu tubuh, reaksi, memori, dan nyeri otot; nafsu makan atau rasa lapar nggak pernah diukur di laporan ini.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena datanya nggak ada di teks; “False” salah karena teks juga nggak nyatain kebalikannya, cuma diam.

author: a health science writer
setting: a football academy studied for ten weeks

title: Apprenticeship or Degree: Comparing Two Routes
text:
School leavers are frequently told that a degree is the safe route and an apprenticeship the practical one. The comparison is lazier than it sounds, because the two paths differ less in reputation than in the moment they force a decision. One of them purchases time; the other purchases experience.
Begin with money. An apprentice earns from the first month and finishes with no debt, while a graduate spends three or four years paying to study. Ten years later the picture alters in certain fields. Graduates in engineering and health tend to reach higher wages, whereas in software and building work the two groups end up close. The risk of regret is genuine on both sides, and neither route removes it entirely. Now consider flexibility. A degree in a broad subject leaves several doors open, while an apprenticeship trains you deeply for one trade and may be harder to leave at twenty-eight.
The correct choice depends on how certain you already are. If you know the work you want and can learn inside it, the apprenticeship route wastes fewer years. If your interests are still moving, paying for time to explore is not weakness but sense. What both routes share is the part nobody advertises. Employers increasingly value evidence of learning rather than the document itself. Whichever you select, you will continue learning long after the certificate arrives.
qs: What is the writer's purpose in this feature?
to show that apprentices avoid debt and so choose better
to show that a degree still opens more doors for everyone
to show that the route depends on the wages a field pays
to show that the right route depends on the reader's certainty

qs.evidence: The correct choice depends on how certain you already are.
qs.answer: to show that the right route depends on the reader's certainty
qs.why: Teks nutup perbandingannya sama “The correct choice depends on how certain you already are”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya simpulan yang wajar dari perbandingan dua jalur, tapi teks ngeblok: “The risk of regret is genuine on both sides” nolak klaim apprentice otomatis milih lebih baik; pintu yang lebih banyak cuma satu sisi neraca; dan upah per bidang disebut cuma buat nunjukin gambarannya campur (“the two groups end up close”), sementara patokan yang dipakai penulis adalah tingkat kepastian pembaca.

qs: Taken together, what does the article say about pay ten years after either route?
it tends to be higher for the apprentice
it is much the same in every trade and subject
it drops for graduates working in health care
it varies with the field of work concerned

qs.evidence: Graduates in engineering and health tend to reach higher wages, whereas in software and building work the two groups end up close.
qs.answer: it varies with the field of work concerned
qs.why: Setelah sepuluh tahun, lulusan teknik dan kesehatan cenderung berupah lebih tinggi, sementara di software dan konstruksi kedua kelompok berdekatan — jadi hasilnya tergantung bidang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Apprentice nggak digambarkan unggul di semua bidang; kesamaan upah cuma berlaku di dua bidang yang disebut, bukan di semua; dan lulusan kesehatan justru contoh yang upahnya naik, bukan turun.

qs: How do the two routes compare on keeping options open?
a trade keeps more doors open because the training is paid
a broad degree keeps more doors open in later years
both routes keep the same number of doors open later
neither route keeps a door open once you turn twenty-eight

qs.evidence: A degree in a broad subject leaves several doors open, while an apprenticeship trains you deeply for one trade and may be harder to leave at twenty-eight.
qs.answer: a broad degree keeps more doors open in later years
qs.why: Teks nyebut gelar di bidang luas “leaves several doors open”, sedangkan apprenticeship melatih satu keahlian dalam-dalam dan “may be harder to leave at twenty-eight”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya cara wajar buat ngomongin keluwesan karier, tapi teks ngeblok: upah sejak bulan pertama disebut sebagai keunggulan uang, bukan keluwesan, dan jalur keahlian justru “harder to leave”; dua jalur juga nggak digambarkan setara di soal pintu; dan “may be harder” cuma nyebut lebih berat, bukan nutup pindah jalur di umur dua puluh delapan.

qs: What does the writer imply about a reader who is still unsure of a career?
such a reader should pick a trade and settle the question
such a reader should choose whichever route costs the least
such a reader can sensibly pay for time to explore
such a reader should postpone both routes for a year

qs.evidence: If your interests are still moving, paying for time to explore is not weakness but sense.
qs.answer: such a reader can sensibly pay for time to explore
qs.why: Teks bilang “If your interests are still moving, paying for time to explore is not weakness but sense”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya nasihat yang biasa dikasih ke lulusan sekolah, tapi teks ngeblok: milih satu keahlian cepat-cepat disyaratkan “If you know the work you want”, jadi bukan buat yang masih ragu; patokan yang dipakai penulis bukan mana yang termurah tapi seberapa yakin kamu; dan nggak ada satu kalimat pun soal menunda dua jalur selama setahun.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "An apprentice leaves training owing money for the course."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: An apprentice leaves training owing money for the course.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: An apprentice earns from the first month and finishes with no debt, while a graduate spends three or four years paying to study.
qs.why: Teks nyebut apprentice selesai tanpa utang, jadi klaim soal ninggalin pelatihan sambil nanggung utang itu kebalikan langsung.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena bertentangan sama teks; “Not stated” salah karena posisi utang apprentice disebut jelas.

author: a careers adviser
setting: a careers feature for school leavers

title: We Should Stop Paying for Speed We Do Not Need
text:
I ordered a phone charger last Tuesday and it arrived the same evening. I did not require it that evening. Nobody asked me whether I did, because the shop's app had already selected the fastest option on my behalf. Somewhere between convenience and habit we have accepted a promise that costs far more than the delivery fee suggests.
The bill is paid by other people. Same-day delivery produces half-empty vans, drivers working to a timetable they cannot control, and packaging chosen for speed rather than weight. A parcel despatched within two hours may travel in a van carrying six items, whereas a parcel despatched within three days travels with two hundred. The saving in time belongs to me alone. The additional fuel, the additional traffic, and the pressure on the driver are shared by everybody in the district.
The remedy is not to shame shoppers. Make the slower option the default, display the difference in plain language at the moment of payment, and offer a modest credit to customers who wait. Where retailers have attempted this, the majority of buyers selected the slower box without complaint. I want an online market that treats patience as normal rather than as a setting you must hunt for. Speed should be something we request, not something we are given.
qs: Taken together, what claim does this column build about the price of fast delivery?
a two-hour parcel shares its van with far fewer other items
the cost of fast delivery is carried by other people
most buyers chose the slower box once retailers offered it
the choice of speed is made by the app rather than the buyer

qs.evidence: The saving in time belongs to me alone.
qs.answer: the cost of fast delivery is carried by other people
qs.why: Kolomnya nyebut “The saving in time belongs to me alone” sementara bahan bakar, kemacetan, dan tekanan ke kurir ditanggung seluruh distrik.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh adalah klaim nyata dari paragraf lain kolom ini, tetapi masing-masing pendukung, bukan hujahnya. Perbandingan enam barang dengan dua ratus barang adalah bukti untuk klaim biaya. Pilihan pembeli pada kotak yang lebih lambat termasuk bagian obat, bukan tesis. Aplikasi yang memilih tanpa bertanya adalah anekdot pembuka. Penekanannya ada pada "The bill is paid by other people" dan "The saving in time belongs to me alone". Opsi terakhir berbentuk rangkuman pula, tetapi aplikasi yang memilih lebih dulu hanya anekdot pembuka; kolom ini menutup dengan siapa yang menanggung ongkosnya.

qs: Which supporting detail shows how a same-day order pushes part of its bill onto other people?
its packaging is chosen for speed rather than for weight
its packaging is chosen to protect goods that break easily
its packaging is heavier than the packaging used on slow orders
its packaging is designed to cut the waste left at the depot

qs.evidence: Same-day delivery produces half-empty vans, drivers working to a timetable they cannot control, and packaging chosen for speed rather than weight.
qs.answer: its packaging is chosen for speed rather than for weight
qs.why: Daftar biaya bersama di teks: van setengah kosong, pengemudi terikat jadwal, dan kemasan “chosen for speed rather than weight” — tiga hal yang dibayar orang lain, bukan pembeli.
qs.whyOthersFail: Perlindungan barang mudah pecah dan pengurangan sampah di depo nggak pernah disebut sebagai alasan pemilihan kemasan. Berat kemasan pengiriman lambat juga nggak pernah dibandingkan; yang disebut cuma bahwa kemasan cepat dipilih demi kecepatan, bukan demi bobot.

qs: How does a two-hour parcel compare with a three-day parcel?
the two-hour parcel travels with about two hundred other items
the two-hour parcel weighs less than the three-day one does
the two-hour parcel shares its van with far fewer items
the two-hour parcel costs the shop nothing extra to send

qs.evidence: A parcel despatched within two hours may travel in a van carrying six items, whereas a parcel despatched within three days travels with two hundred.
qs.answer: the two-hour parcel shares its van with far fewer items
qs.why: Paket dua jam bisa jalan di van berisi enam barang sementara paket tiga hari jalan bareng dua ratus barang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya perbandingan yang masuk akal antara kirim cepat dan kirim lambat, tapi teks ngeblok: angka dua ratus itu milik paket tiga hari, bukan paket dua jam; bobot paketnya nggak pernah dibandingkan, yang dibandingkan jumlah barang per van; dan “The additional fuel, the additional traffic” nunjukin ada tambahan biaya, bukan nol.

qs: Which statement best restates what the writer wants shops to do?
make the slow option standard and reward those who wait
make the slow option standard and charge extra for speed
make the fast option standard but show its cost clearly
make the slow option standard and drop the fastest choice

qs.evidence: Make the slower option the default, display the difference in plain language at the moment of payment, and offer a modest credit to customers who wait.
qs.answer: make the slow option standard and reward those who wait
qs.why: Usulannya persis tiga hal: jadikan opsi lambat sebagai default, tampilkan bedanya dengan bahasa jelas saat bayar, dan “offer a modest credit to customers who wait”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya kebijakan toko yang masuk akal, tapi teks ngeblok: yang ditawarkan “a modest credit to customers who wait”, bukan tarif tambahan buat yang mau cepat; default yang diminta justru opsi lambat, bukan opsi cepat; dan “Speed should be something we request” nunjukin opsi cepat tetap ada, cuma nggak dikasih otomatis.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Where shops tried the idea, most customers accepted the slower delivery."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Where shops tried the idea, most customers accepted the slower delivery.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Where retailers have attempted this, the majority of buyers selected the slower box without complaint.
qs.why: “the majority of buyers” sama artinya sama “most customers”, dan teks nyebut mereka milih kotak yang lebih lambat tanpa protes.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” salah karena nggak ada proposisi yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena hasil percobaan retailer itu disebut langsung.

topic: fast delivery and its hidden costs
author: a consumer affairs columnist
setting: an opinion column about online shopping

title: Why So Many Apps Ask for the Address Book
text:
A team of student researchers examined the permission requests of 200 free apps in order to discover what drives them. They did not inspect the code; instead they read every privacy notice and every request screen, then wrote to the developers. Ninety-two firms replied. The pattern that emerged had less to do with features than with revenue.
Two thirds of the apps requested the contact list, yet only a quarter used it for anything a user would notice. Where the request appeared, an advertising partner was named in the notice nine times out of ten. Developers explained the logic plainly. A network of contacts helps advertisers estimate who else might purchase, so the partner pays more for that space. The request therefore follows the business model, and the feature is invented afterwards to justify it.
The study suggests a simple test for readers. Ask what the app would lose if it never saw your contact list, then compare that answer with the section on partners. Where the two answers disagree, refusing the request costs you very little. The researchers also want app stores to place the reason for each request beside the button. Permission screens are cheap to write, whereas explanations are what actually alter behaviour. Regulators in two countries are already considering such a requirement.
qs: What is the purpose of this report?
to explain what the contact request is really for
to explain which features genuinely need a user's contact list
to explain how advertising partners keep the contacts they collect
to explain how app stores check permissions before release

qs.evidence: The pattern that emerged had less to do with features than with revenue.
qs.answer: to explain what the contact request is really for
qs.why: Pola yang muncul disebut “had less to do with features than with revenue”, jadi laporan ini nerangin apa sebenarnya yang ada di balik permintaan daftar kontak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya topik yang wajar buat laporan privasi, tapi teks ngeblok: fiturnya disebut “invented afterwards to justify it”, jadi laporan nggak nyusun daftar fitur yang benar-benar butuh kontak; cara mitra iklan nyimpen data nggak pernah diperiksa (“They did not inspect the code”); dan app store cuma diminta nulis alasan di sebelah tombol, bukan digambarkan sedang memeriksa izin.

qs: Taken together, how many of the 200 firms answered the researchers' letters?
about two thirds of the total number
exactly nine out of every ten firms
slightly fewer than a hundred
a quarter of the firms in the study

qs.evidence: Ninety-two firms replied.
qs.answer: slightly fewer than a hundred
qs.why: Teks nyebut 92 perusahaan menjawab, jadi sedikit di bawah seratus dari 200 yang dihubungi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dua per tiga itu porsi aplikasi yang minta daftar kontak; sembilan dari sepuluh adalah seberapa sering mitra iklan disebut di notis; dan seperempat adalah porsi aplikasi yang benar-benar memakai kontak buat fitur yang kelihatan.

qs: Which finding best supports the claim that money drives the request?
two thirds of the apps requested the user's contact list
a quarter used the list for something a user notices
ninety-two of the two hundred firms answered the letters
nearly every such request listed a company that buys space

qs.evidence: Where the request appeared, an advertising partner was named in the notice nine times out of ten.
qs.answer: nearly every such request listed a company that buys space
qs.why: Di mana permintaan itu muncul, mitra iklan disebut dalam notis sembilan dari sepuluh kali — kaitan langsung antara permintaan dan uang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya angka asli dari studi ini, tapi nggak satu pun nyambungin permintaan ke uang: dua per tiga cuma ngukur seberapa umum permintaannya; seperempat yang memakainya buat fitur kelihatan nunjukin permintaannya sering nggak perlu, bukan alasannya; dan 92 firma yang menjawab itu ukuran metode, bukan temuan.

qs: Which conclusion about contact-list features do the developers' own explanations lead to?
such features are usually invented afterwards to justify the request
such features are noticed by most of the people who install the app
such features are built before the privacy notice is drafted
such features are what persuade an advertising partner to pay more

qs.evidence: The request therefore follows the business model, and the feature is invented afterwards to justify it.
qs.answer: such features are usually invented afterwards to justify the request
qs.why: Rantainya lengkap di teks: dua per tiga aplikasi minta daftar kontak, cuma seperempat memakainya untuk hal yang disadari pengguna, dan penjelasan pengembang berujung pada “the feature is invented afterwards to justify it”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Teks menyediakan angka yang menolak tiap pengecoh. “Only a quarter used it for anything a user would notice” membantah bahwa fiturnya disadari sebagian besar pengguna. Urutan yang disebut teks kebalikan dari opsi ketiga: permintaan dulu, fitur menyusul. Dan yang bikin mitra iklan bayar lebih mahal adalah “A network of contacts”, bukan fiturnya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "All of the firms contacted by the researchers sent a reply."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: All of the firms contacted by the researchers sent a reply.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: A team of student researchers examined the permission requests of 200 free apps in order to discover what drives them.
qs.why: Dari 200 aplikasi yang diperiksa cuma 92 firma yang jawab, jadi klaim “all of the firms” bertentangan sama angka di teks.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena jumlah yang balas jauh di bawah total; “Not stated” salah karena jumlah pembalas ditulis jelas.

author: a science journalist
setting: a popular report on a student research project

title: Reviewing the City's New Travel Card App
text:
The city transport office has replaced its paper tickets with an app. After three weeks of daily use I can report that it is both better and worse than the system it removed. Purchasing a journey now takes eleven seconds instead of a queue. Losing your battery, however, now removes your ticket as well.
The advantages are genuine. The map displays the next three buses at a chosen stop. The fare is charged at the cheaper weekly rate automatically, and a single tap transfers a monthly pass to a new handset. Reliability, though, is uneven. Twice in three weeks the app refused to open underground, where there is no signal, and the offline ticket it promises required four attempts to appear. Elderly passengers at my stop have quietly returned to purchasing paper from the driver, a habit the office intends to end in June.
So is the app worth installing? For anyone travelling daily with a modern phone, certainly; the weekly limit alone repays the effort. For occasional riders, and for anyone whose handset is five years old, the app removes a functioning system and offers a fragile one. My verdict is three marks out of five. It would deserve four if the office retained paper tickets for the passengers who depend on them.
qs: Taken together, what overall verdict does the reviewer reach on the travel card app?
the fare is charged at the cheaper weekly rate without asking
handy for daily riders, risky for occasional ones
the app refused to open underground, where there is no signal
the loss of paper tickets is the change that hurts most

qs.evidence: My verdict is three marks out of five.
qs.answer: handy for daily riders, risky for occasional ones
qs.why: Nilai “three marks out of five” itu hasil penimbangan: berguna banget buat yang naik tiap hari dengan ponsel baru, rapuh buat penumpang sesekali dan ponsel tua.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh betul-betul tercatat dalam ulasan ini, tetapi masing-masing satu butir untung atau satu butir rugi, bukan putusan menyeluruhnya. Tarif mingguan otomatis adalah salah satu keunggulan. Kegagalan membuka di bawah tanah adalah satu contoh keandalan yang timpang. Penumpang tua yang kembali ke tiket kertas adalah akibat yang dicatat, lalu dipakai di kalimat penutup sebagai syarat nilai keempat. Putusannya sendiri berbunyi "it is both better and worse than the system it removed", dengan pemilahan harian berbanding sesekali. Opsi terakhir berbentuk putusan, tetapi hanya menimbang satu sisi; ulasan ini menyatakan "it is both better and worse than the system it removed".

qs: Taken together, what does the review say happened when the app was opened underground?
it refused to start on two occasions
it opened but lost the offline ticket
it opened after a delay of three minutes
it opened normally on every journey

qs.evidence: Twice in three weeks the app refused to open underground, where there is no signal, and the offline ticket it promises required four attempts to appear.
qs.answer: it refused to start on two occasions
qs.why: Dua kali dalam tiga minggu aplikasinya nolak kebuka di bawah tanah, tempat yang nggak ada sinyal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Aplikasinya bukan cuma lambat atau kehilangan tiket luring, dan jelas bukan berjalan normal: dua kali dalam tiga pekan dia menolak terbuka di bawah tanah karena nggak ada sinyal.

qs: How does the app compare with the paper system for older passengers?
the app now suits them better than paper does
the app has already replaced paper at their stop
paper still suits them better for the time being
paper and the app suit them about equally well

qs.evidence: Elderly passengers at my stop have quietly returned to purchasing paper from the driver, a habit the office intends to end in June.
qs.answer: paper still suits them better for the time being
qs.why: Penumpang lanjut usia di pemberhentian penulis “quietly returned to purchasing paper from the driver”, jadi sistem kertas masih lebih pas buat mereka.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya kesimpulan yang masuk akal soal penumpang tua dan teknologi baru, tapi teks ngeblok: mereka justru balik ke kertas, jadi aplikasinya belum lebih cocok dan belum menggantikan kertas di pemberhentian itu; dan penulis mau kertas dipertahankan “for the passengers who depend on them”, jadi kedua sistem nggak setara buat mereka.

qs: What does the reviewer imply about the decision to withdraw paper tickets?
some passengers may lose an option they can rely on
queues at the stops may return once paper disappears
the office may raise the weekly limit for those passengers
the office may restore paper tickets again next year

qs.evidence: It would deserve four if the office retained paper tickets for the passengers who depend on them.
qs.answer: some passengers may lose an option they can rely on
qs.why: Penulis bilang aplikasinya layak empat “if the office retained paper tickets for the passengers who depend on them”, jadi penghapusan kertas nyabut pilihan yang bisa diandalkan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya akibat yang masuk akal dari penghapusan tiket kertas, tapi teks ngeblok: pembelian di aplikasi disebut “eleven seconds instead of a queue”, jadi antrean bukan yang balik; batas mingguan cuma disebut sebagai keuntungan yang udah otomatis, bukan hal yang mau diubah; dan kantor justru berniat “to end in June”, bukan mengembalikan kertas tahun depan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The app works out the cheaper weekly fare for the passenger."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The app works out the cheaper weekly fare for the passenger.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The fare is charged at the cheaper weekly rate automatically, and a single tap transfers a monthly pass to a new handset.
qs.why: Teks nyebut tarif otomatis dihitung pada rate mingguan yang lebih murah, jadi klaim ini cuma parafrasa fitur itu.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” salah karena nggak ada yang dibalik; “Not stated” salah karena fitur tarif mingguan disebut jelas.

author: a daily bus passenger
setting: a review of a city travel app

title: Privacy Belongs on the Timetable
text:
Our school teaches pupils how to compose a formal letter, how to interpret a graph, and how to swim. It teaches nothing whatever about the exchange they make daily when they open an app. That gap is not a minor one, and pretending it belongs to parents alone has ceased to be honest.
The problem appears in ordinary questions I cannot answer for my class. Why does a free game request the microphone? What does a shop learn from a loyalty card, and who else receives it? Pupils are not careless; they simply possess no vocabulary for the thing being taken. A survey of our own Year Ten discovered that most could name a virus, yet almost none could explain the function of an advertising identifier.
A remedy would fit inside the existing timetable. Six lessons a year, taught in the subject where devices are already used, would cover permissions, passwords, data brokers, and the right to ask what a company holds. Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher. What it demands is the decision that this counts as literacy. Employers, regulators and universities all assume this knowledge already exists. Until we reach that decision, we are teaching children to read every text except the one they agree to every day.
qs: What is the writer's purpose in this article?
to argue that parents should teach this subject at home
to argue that pupils are careless with their own data
to argue that schools need new equipment for these lessons
to argue that privacy lessons belong on the school timetable

qs.evidence: What it demands is the decision that this counts as literacy.
qs.answer: to argue that privacy lessons belong on the school timetable
qs.why: Penulis minta “the decision that this counts as literacy”, yaitu privasi masuk jadwal pelajaran resmi.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya posisi yang wajar dalam debat pendidikan digital, tapi teks ngeblok: “pretending it belongs to parents alone has ceased to be honest” nolak penyerahan ke rumah; “Pupils are not careless” nolak tuduhan ke murid; dan “Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher” nolak tuntutan alat baru.

qs: Which finding about Year Ten backs the writer's call for privacy lessons on the timetable?
most could name a virus, yet almost none could explain an advertising identifier
most could explain an advertising identifier, yet few could name a virus
most asked for lessons on passwords rather than lessons on games
most said their parents had already explained app permissions to them

qs.evidence: A survey of our own Year Ten discovered that most could name a virus, yet almost none could explain the function of an advertising identifier.
qs.answer: most could name a virus, yet almost none could explain an advertising identifier
qs.why: Survei Year Ten menguatkan gagasan utama: murid punya kosakata untuk ancaman lama (virus) tapi nggak punya kata untuk hal yang tiap hari mereka serahkan, jadi celahnya memang di kurikulum.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi kedua membalik hasil survei. Permintaan pelajaran kata sandi nggak pernah disurvei — kata sandi cuma muncul di daftar isi usulan enam pelajaran. Dan teks justru bilang menganggap urusan ini milik orang tua “has ceased to be honest”, bukan bahwa orang tua udah menjelaskannya.

qs: Which point best supports the claim that the change would be cheap?
the plan needs no fresh equipment and no extra teacher
employers and universities assume the knowledge already exists
most Year Ten pupils could name a virus by itself
the school already teaches letters, graphs, and swimming

qs.evidence: Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher.
qs.answer: the plan needs no fresh equipment and no extra teacher
qs.why: Kalimat “Nothing here demands new equipment or an additional teacher” persis nunjukin usulannya nggak nambah biaya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya beneran ada di teks dan kedengaran mendukung, tapi nggak ngomongin biaya: anggapan employer dan universitas nunjukin kenapa pelajarannya perlu; kemampuan nyebut virus ngukur pengetahuan murid; dan daftar surat, grafik, dan renang cuma nunjukin apa yang udah diajarkan sekolah.

qs: What does the writer imply about pupils who accept every permission?
they lack the words for what they are handing over
they are less careful than the pupils above them
they have been warned about this at home already
they understand the trade but decide to ignore it

qs.evidence: Pupils are not careless; they simply possess no vocabulary for the thing being taken.
qs.answer: they lack the words for what they are handing over
qs.why: Teks nyebut “Pupils are not careless; they simply possess no vocabulary for the thing being taken”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya penjelasan yang masuk akal soal remaja dan izin aplikasi, tapi teks ngeblok: “Pupils are not careless” nolak tuduhan kurang hati-hati dan nggak ada perbandingan antar tingkatan; peringatan dari rumah nggak pernah disebut ada, malah keluarga dibilang nggak bisa ditinggali urusan ini sendiri; dan kalau mereka paham pertukarannya, kalimat soal ketiadaan kosakata jadi nggak masuk akal.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer's school already teaches two of the six proposed lessons."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer's school already teaches two of the six proposed lessons.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: Six lessons a year, taught in the subject where devices are already used, would cover permissions, passwords, data brokers, and the right to ask what a company holds.
qs.why: Teks cuma ngusulin enam pelajaran baru dan nyebut sekolah belum ngajarin apa pun soal itu; jumlah yang “udah diajarkan” nggak pernah dirinci.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena angka itu nggak ada di teks; “False” salah karena teks nggak nyatain kebalikannya secara spesifik, cuma diam soal rincian itu.

author: a secondary school teacher
setting: an opinion piece by a classroom teacher

title: Part-time Work and School Marks: How Many Hours?
text:
Does a weekend job damage school results? Earlier investigations had produced contradictory conclusions on the question. A three-year study of 1,200 pupils in nine schools suggests that the answer depends almost entirely on the number of hours. The researchers followed the same learners from Year Ten to the end of Year Twelve and compared their marks with records of paid work.
Up to eight hours a week, working pupils performed slightly better than those without employment at all. Their teachers described them as better organized and noticeably more willing to plan ahead. Beyond twelve hours the pattern reversed sharply: marks declined, absence increased, and sleep dropped by nearly an hour on working nights. The cause was not the employment itself but what it replaced. Pupils in the heaviest group surrendered revision and rest first, because those were the only parts of the week nobody was paying for.
The report resists a simple rule. Some learners in the long-hours group were supporting families and had no choice, and the study did not measure the value of the money they earned. The authors nevertheless recommend that schools ask about working hours early in the year. They also urge employers of young staff to avoid evening shifts before examinations. The authors describe the relationship as reliable but modest in scale. A small job appears to assist; a second job appears to cost more than it pays.
qs: Taken together, what does this three-year study establish about part-time jobs?
pupils working eight hours or fewer were better organized
the effect of a job depends on the hours worked
the heaviest workers gave up revision and rest before anything else
schools should ask about working hours early in the year

qs.evidence: Earlier investigations had produced contradictory conclusions on the question. A three-year study of 1,200 pupils in nine schools suggests that the answer depends almost entirely on the number of hours.
qs.answer: the effect of a job depends on the hours worked
qs.why: Studi tiga tahun atas 1.200 murid nyimpulin “the answer depends almost entirely on the number of hours”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh adalah pernyataan nyata dari paragraf lain laporan ini, tetapi masing-masing satu sisi temuan atau satu anjuran, bukan temuan pusatnya. Kelompok delapan jam yang lebih tertata adalah separuh pola. Penyerahan waktu ulang kaji dan istirahat adalah mekanismenya, "The cause was not the employment itself but what it replaced". Anjuran agar sekolah bertanya lebih awal adalah rekomendasi. Temuan pusatnya berbunyi "the answer depends almost entirely on the number of hours".

qs: Taken together, what do the figures show about pupils working more than twelve hours a week?
their results fell and their sleep was cut
their marks rose while attendance quietly fell
their teachers found them better organized
their families reported no change at all

qs.evidence: Beyond twelve hours the pattern reversed sharply: marks declined, absence increased, and sleep dropped by nearly an hour on working nights.
qs.answer: their results fell and their sleep was cut
qs.why: Di atas dua belas jam pola berbalik tajam: nilai turun, absen naik, dan tidur berkurang hampir satu jam pada malam kerja.
qs.whyOthersFail: Nilai mereka turun, bukan naik; pujian soal kerapian justru buat kelompok di bawah delapan jam; dan laporan keluarga nggak pernah dikutip di teks.

qs: Which explanation does the report give for the fall in marks?
the pupils were working evening shifts before examinations
study time and sleep were dropped before anything else
the work itself left those pupils physically tired
those pupils were already behind before they started work

qs.evidence: Pupils in the heaviest group surrendered revision and rest first, because those were the only parts of the week nobody was paying for.
qs.answer: study time and sleep were dropped before anything else
qs.why: Teks nyebut kelompok jam terberat “surrendered revision and rest first, because those were the only parts of the week nobody was paying for”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya sebab yang masuk akal buat nilai yang jatuh, tapi teks ngeblok: shift malam sebelum ujian cuma imbauan laporan buat pemberi kerja, bukan temuan; “The cause was not the employment itself but what it replaced” nolak kelelahan kerja sebagai sebab; dan nggak ada data yang bilang kelompok itu udah tertinggal sebelum bekerja.

qs: What does the report imply about pupils who work long hours from necessity?
their results may improve once the hours fall next year
their marks may have fallen less than the others' marks
their schools might already have offered them extra support
the study's figures may not capture their position

qs.evidence: Some learners in the long-hours group were supporting families and had no choice, and the study did not measure the value of the money they earned.
qs.answer: the study's figures may not capture their position
qs.why: Sebagian murid jam panjang “were supporting families and had no choice”, sementara nilai uang yang mereka dapat nggak diukur — jadi angka studi nggak nangkep keadaan mereka.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiganya dugaan yang masuk akal soal murid yang kerja karena keharusan, tapi teks ngeblok: laporan nggak meramal jamnya bakal turun tahun depan; nilai kelompok ini nggak dipisah dari kelompok jam panjang lain, jadi nggak bisa dibilang turunnya lebih sedikit; dan bantuan sekolah nggak pernah disebut — yang disebut “the study did not measure the value of the money they earned”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The study followed the pupils for a single school year."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The study followed the pupils for a single school year.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: The researchers followed the same learners from Year Ten to the end of Year Twelve and compared their marks with records of paid work.
qs.why: Teks nyebut penelitian jalan tiga tahun, dari Year Ten sampai akhir Year Twelve, jadi klaim satu tahun ngebalik durasinya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” salah karena durasinya tiga tahun; “Not stated” salah karena rentang tahunnya ditulis jelas.

author: an education researcher
setting: a three-year study in nine secondary schools

title: Gym Membership or the Park: Which Habit Lasts?
text:
Two acquaintances resolved to become fit in January. Their experiment was accidental, yet it illustrates a genuine dilemma. One purchased a year at a gym; the other acquired a pair of shoes and began running in the park. A year later both were fitter, yet their reasons for continuing were entirely different, and that difference matters more than any comparison of equipment.
The gym offers structure. Machines guide the movement, an instructor corrects mistakes, and severe weather becomes irrelevant. In exchange it charges a monthly fee and demands a journey, which is the point at which most memberships quietly die. Park running costs almost nothing and starts at the front door, yet it provides no instruction, punishes poor shoes, and disappears in heavy rain. Neither arrangement guarantees continued attendance beyond the initial enthusiasm. Strength is easier to build indoors, whereas the habit itself is easier to build outdoors, because the barrier is lower on a tired evening.
If your aim is muscle, or you need supervision after an injury, the fee purchases something real. If your aim is a routine you will maintain in October as well as January, the cheaper option is usually the stronger one. The honest advice is to choose according to the obstacle rather than the ambition. Motivation, in other words, responds to circumstances rather than to intentions. Ask what will stop you in month four, then select the option that removes it.
qs: What is the writer's main purpose in this feature?
