Visitors largely decide what counts as traditional, and communities perform to match.

qs.evidence: Once a word begins selling merchandise its meaning becomes a cost to be reduced, and reduction continues until the label may be attached to almost anything without provoking laughter.
qs.answer: A word put to work selling things loses precision until it fits almost anything.
qs.why: Kalimat itu memberi mekanismenya: begitu sebuah kata dipakai berjualan, maknanya menjadi biaya yang dipotong terus sampai labelnya bisa ditempel ke apa saja tanpa memancing tawa.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menggambarkan penjual masuk akal untuk kata iklan mana pun, tetapi teks menyebut yang menyusut adalah daya bedanya, “its meaning becomes a cost to be reduced”; opsi juru masak yang tampak mahal dibuka paragraf tiga dengan “What interests me is the identity of whoever eventually pays”, jadi akibat, bukan argumennya; opsi komunitas yang berlakon dibuka “A subtler indignity accompanies the commercial one”, yang menempatkannya sebagai tambahan.

qs: What can be inferred from the two pricing moves described in the third paragraph?
The price signal is read backwards, so the honest cook looks like the greedy one.
Both prices may be read as quality, and the chain will follow by raising its own.
Customers can seldom tell the kitchens apart, though price is the signal left to them.
Her higher price protects her, since buyers will pay more for a traceable recipe.

qs.evidence: She raises her prices to signal quality, which makes her appear expensive, while the chain lowers its prices and consequently appears generous.
qs.answer: The price signal is read backwards, so the honest cook looks like the greedy one.
qs.why: Dua gerakan harga itu diberi akibat yang terbalik dari maksudnya: naiknya harga membuat dia tampak mahal, turunnya harga membuat jaringan tampak baik hati.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi kedua harga sebagai bukti mutu bertabrakan dengan kalimat itu, yang menyebut jaringan justru menurunkan harganya; opsi pembeli yang tak bisa membedakan menghapus inti kalimatnya, sebab sinyal harganya terbaca, hanya terbaca terbalik; opsi harga tinggi yang melindungi juru masak bertabrakan dengan “Customers depart persuaded that they have supported tradition”.

qs: What feeling does the writer convey through the story of the withdrawn dish?
Measured regret at a kitchen obliged to follow the taste of its customers.
Quiet outrage that outsiders now decide what counts as genuine cooking.
Wry sympathy for tourists unable to tell the traditional from the invented.
Guarded optimism that the dish will return once the fashion has passed.

qs.evidence: A friend who runs a modest kitchen in Yogyakarta recently withdrew a dish her family had eaten for generations, because tourists complained repeatedly that it did not taste traditional enough.
qs.answer: Quiet outrage that outsiders now decide what counts as genuine cooking.
qs.why: Hidangan yang dimakan keluarga itu selama beberapa generasi ditarik karena keluhan turis, dan teks menyebutnya justru tradisional; di situ ada kemarahan yang ditahan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi penyesalan terukur meredakan penilaian teks yang menyebut keluhan turis salah; opsi simpati pada turis salah pihak karena mereka pihak yang menuntut; opsi optimisme berhati-hati menambahkan harapan yang nggak ada di paragraf itu.

qs: What does it mean that the chain "purchased her adjective wholesale"?
It bought the word in bulk, as though the adjective came in sacks.
It took the word over entirely, as though no permission were required.
It resold the word to other kitchens, as though it held a licence.
It used the word only among traders, never printing it on a menu.

qs.evidence: The cook whose family actually preserved the recipe now competes against a chain that purchased her adjective wholesale, and she cannot readily complain, since the adjective was never hers to register.
qs.answer: It took the word over entirely, as though no permission were required.
qs.why: Klausa berikutnya, “she cannot readily complain, since the adjective was never hers to register”, memaksa arti yang bukan arti dagang: kata itu diambil habis tanpa izin, karena nggak ada izin yang bisa diminta.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi mendefinisikan “wholesale” dengan presisi yang sama dan memakai rangka “as though” yang sama, masing-masing untuk satu arti sah kata itu. Opsi membeli borongan dalam karung memakai arti dagang yang paling umum, padahal yang “dibeli” di kalimat ini kata sifat, bukan barang, dan kalimatnya menutup dengan “the adjective was never hers to register”. Opsi menjual kata itu kembali kepada dapur lain menambahkan transaksi yang nggak ada di teks. Opsi hanya dipakai antar pedagang bertabrakan dengan paragraf satu, di mana label itu terpampang di menu dan pada kemasan biskuit.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer sets out a detailed plan for repairing the problem."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer sets out a detailed plan for repairing the problem.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: I possess no elegant remedy, and I distrust essays that arrive brandishing one.
qs.why: Dia justru bilang nggak punya obat yang rapi dan curiga pada esai yang menawarkannya. Klaim ini bertolak belakang.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertentangan dengan kalimat itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena penulis menyatakan posisinya sendiri.

topic: how the word authentic lost its meaning in food marketing
author: Elang Wicaksana
setting: a critical essay on authenticity and commerce

title: Five Tired People in a Room
text:
The shortlist appears in October, and for a fortnight the entire literary economy behaves as though six novels had been selected by physics rather than by five tired individuals in a room above a bank. Sales multiply immediately, and booksellers construct elaborate pyramids beside the entrance. Interviewers enquire, with touching sincerity, what the shortlisting means to the author, and the author replies that awards are not the point, which is true and yet somehow said into a microphone.

I have judged a modest regional prize twice, so my scepticism is at least paid for by experience. The process is not corrupt; it is merely human, which is considerably more unpredictable. A book that nobody loves may survive because nobody hates it either, while the volume that split the panel down the middle dies of its own electricity. Compromise favours competence, and competence is the least interesting quality any novel can possess.

The genuine damage occurs afterwards, in the reading public rather than the panel. A prize does not merely reward a book; it abolishes several hundred others for the season, since attention is finite and shelves are not elastic. Publishers observe which qualities travelled well and commission accordingly, so the next few years arrive faintly perfumed with imitation. Nobody plans this. It emerges from a thousand reasonable decisions taken by employees protecting their livelihoods.

Defenders of the system reply that prizes create readers, and the reply deserves respect rather than mockery. Somebody who buys one shortlisted novel every autumn has a richer inner life than somebody who buys none, and I have never met a writer whose rent was paid by principle. The awkward truth is that both propositions hold simultaneously. Prizes widen the audience and narrow the field, and the second effect operates slowly enough to be denied by anybody who profits from the first.

What I would like is not abolition but modesty in the surrounding language. Announce the winner as the preference of five particular readers in a particular month, which is precisely what it is, and permit the losing novels to remain unfinished business rather than settled cases. The last time I served, we changed our minds three times in ninety minutes and then announced our verdict with the composure of a jury. Somebody in the audience wept audibly. I recall wondering whether she would have wept for our second preference, and concluding, uncomfortably, that she almost certainly would.
qs: Read as a whole, which position does the writer end up defending?
The panel is not corrupt but human, and human is a great deal less predictable.
The announcement should name a winner and let the losing novels be treated as settled cases.
Awards bring in more readers while quietly shrinking what gets written next.
Compromise favours competence, though competence is the dullest thing a novel has.

qs.evidence: Prizes widen the audience and narrow the field, and the second effect operates slowly enough to be denied by anybody who profits from the first.
qs.answer: Awards bring in more readers while quietly shrinking what gets written next.
qs.why: Kalimat sebelumnya menyebut “The awkward truth is that both propositions hold simultaneously”, lalu kalimat ini merumuskan keduanya: pembaca bertambah, ragam yang ditulis menyempit.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi panel manusiawi dan opsi kompromi sama-sama kalimat asli paragraf dua, tetapi keduanya menggambarkan proses di dalam ruangan, sedangkan teks menyebut “The genuine damage occurs afterwards, in the reading public rather than the panel”; opsi bahasa yang lebih sederhana dibuka “What I would like is not abolition but modesty in the surrounding language”, jadi tuntutan yang menyusul argumennya, bukan argumennya. | "The announcement should name a winner and let..." is wrong: blocked directly by 'permit the losing novels to remain unfinished business rather than settled cases'

qs: What can be inferred about the way panels arrive at a shortlist?
Panels may reward the novel that split them, since disagreement signals ambition.
A book survives by having one judge prepared to fight for it to the very end.
Judges tire, and tiredness tends to settle on whichever case is quickest.
Books that provoke the strongest reactions are the ones most likely to be dropped.

qs.evidence: A book that nobody loves may survive because nobody hates it either, while the volume that split the panel down the middle dies of its own electricity.
qs.answer: Books that provoke the strongest reactions are the ones most likely to be dropped.
qs.why: Kalimatnya memasangkan dua nasib: yang nggak dibenci siapa pun lolos, yang membelah panel mati karena listriknya sendiri. Reaksi kuat merugikan sebuah novel.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi buku yang membelah panel dimenangkan justru kebalikan dari klausa kedua kalimat itu, “dies of its own electricity”; opsi satu juri pembela membaca kelolosan sebagai hasil dukungan, padahal teks menyebut sebabnya ketiadaan pembenci; opsi juri kelelahan memakai kata “tired” dari paragraf satu, tetapi mekanisme yang teks sebut adalah kompromi yang memihak kompetensi.

qs: What does the writer suggest by mentioning the composure of a jury?
That the calm was earned, three changes of mind being what real care looks like.
That a steady public front conceals a distinctly wobbly private process.
That the weeping proved the verdict had landed with genuine weight.
That the courts are no steadier than panels, whichever room they sit in.

qs.evidence: The last time I served, we changed our minds three times in ninety minutes and then announced our verdict with the composure of a jury.
qs.answer: That a steady public front conceals a distinctly wobbly private process.
qs.why: Satu kalimat memasang dua hal berlawanan: tiga kali berubah pikiran dalam sembilan puluh menit, lalu tampil setenang juri. Ketenangan itu dipakai, bukan dimiliki.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh sama tegasnya dengan kunci dan sama-sama sejalan dengan tesis bahwa hadiah diberi wibawa yang berlebihan, tetapi masing-masing salah derajat atau salah sasaran. Opsi ketenangan yang pantas menghapus fungsi kata “composure” sebagai penampilan, dan bertabrakan dengan tuntutan paragraf lima agar pengumuman berhenti berbunyi seperti putusan pengadilan. Opsi tangis penonton sebagai bukti bobot dibalik kalimat penutup, yang menyebut penonton itu hampir pasti akan menangis untuk pilihan kedua. Opsi pengadilan sama goyahnya memindahkan sasaran perbandingannya ke pengadilan, padahal kiasan itu dipakai untuk menilai panel.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the point about shelves in the third paragraph?
Honouring one title pushes rivals out of a limited stock of notice.
Notice is not the scarce thing; shelf space is, though shops may order more.
The pyramids by the entrance do the abolishing, not the prize standing behind them.
Each prize makes its own season, so losing novels may simply wait for the next.

qs.evidence: A prize does not merely reward a book; it abolishes several hundred others for the season, since attention is finite and shelves are not elastic.
qs.answer: Honouring one title pushes rivals out of a limited stock of notice.
qs.why: Klausa sebabnya menyebut perhatian terbatas dan rak nggak elastis, jadi satu pemenang menyingkirkan ratusan judul dari persediaan perhatian yang tetap.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi perhatian yang nggak terbatas bertabrakan dengan “attention is finite” di kalimat yang sama; opsi piramida toko memindahkan sebabnya ke penataan toko, padahal kalimat itu menyebut hadiahnya yang menghapus; opsi menunggu musim berikutnya menambahkan penangguhan yang nggak ada, sebab teks memakai kata “abolishes” untuk musim itu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer has served on a judging panel more than once."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer has served on a judging panel more than once.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: I have judged a modest regional prize twice, so my scepticism is at least paid for by experience.
qs.why: Dia menyebut menjadi juri dua kali, jadi “lebih dari sekali” itu parafrasa yang pas.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan kata “twice”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena pengalamannya ditulis di paragraf dua.

topic: literary prizes and their effect on readers and publishers
author: Ratih Sudarso
setting: a critical essay on book awards

title: Walls With Better Publicity
text:
Somewhere around 2012 the noun collaboration escaped from its dictionary and began appearing in architectural drawings. Partitions were demolished, desks were shoved into clusters, and the resulting expanse was advertised internally as a space engineered for spontaneous encounter. Nobody mentioned the rental cost per square metre, although the arithmetic was transparent to anybody willing to divide. Language had performed its function: an economy measure had been rebranded as a philosophy of openness.

The empirical case against these interiors is now embarrassingly robust, and it was assembled largely by their occupants. Concentration collapses within earshot of a telephone discussion concerning somebody else's dentist. Acoustic complaints dominate every internal survey I have encountered, and management responds with posters recommending mutual consideration. Employees adapt rationally, acquiring enormous headphones and addressing colleagues exclusively in writing, which produces the pleasant spectacle of an open-plan floor in absolute silence, everybody messaging the neighbour opposite. The architecture achieved the reverse of its declared purpose while remaining a triumph of its undeclared one.

What fascinates me is the vocabulary of the defence, which has proved remarkably durable. Objectors are described as resistant to change, a phrase that converts a technical complaint into a defect of personality. Requests for a door become requests for privilege. Meanwhile the executives who commissioned the openness retain their own enclosed suites at the far end of the building, an arrangement nobody has yet described as an obstacle to spontaneous encounter.

The pandemic years supplied an accidental experiment, and its findings embarrassed almost everybody. Offered a genuine choice, most employees preferred to concentrate at home and to commute precisely for the conversations the open plan had promised to manufacture. Presence recovered its value, though for reasons the original design had never anticipated. They wanted a canteen, a corridor and somebody to disagree with over lunch. Nobody had ever wanted to overhear a stranger negotiating a mortgage.

So the desks are being rearranged once more, and a fresh vocabulary already circulates in the trade press. We now construct neighbourhoods, quiet pods and zones of intentional focus, which are partitions with superior publicity. Consultants have rediscovered the wall and are charging handsomely for the discovery. I oppose none of it, and my own department acquired two modest rooms last winter through this linguistic evolution. I would simply like the record to indicate that the partitions vanished for financial reasons and are reappearing for financial reasons, and that the philosophy has been trailing quietly behind the budget throughout, carrying the bags.
qs: How does the writer connect the cost of floor space to the language of openness?
He argues the philosophy came first and the savings arrived later as a bonus.
He treats the talk of openness as cover for a decision about money.
He accepts that openness and cheaper floor space were pursued as one honest aim.
He notes the rent per square metre was published, so nobody could hide behind it.

qs.evidence: Language had performed its function: an economy measure had been rebranded as a philosophy of openness.
qs.answer: He treats the talk of openness as cover for a decision about money.
qs.why: Kalimatnya menyebut langkah penghematan telah dikemas ulang sebagai filosofi keterbukaan, jadi bahasanya bekerja untuk menutupi urutan sebenarnya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi filosofi lebih dulu membalik urutan yang dinyatakan kata “rebranded”; opsi satu tujuan jujur menghapus kata itu juga, sebab pengemasan ulang berarti motifnya digeser, bukan digabung; opsi sewa yang dipublikasikan bertabrakan dengan kalimat “Nobody mentioned the rental cost per square metre”, yang menyebut angkanya hanya bisa dihitung sendiri, bukan diumumkan.

qs: What can be inferred from the position of the executives' own rooms?
Senior staff keep their rooms, though chiefly because confidential business needs a door.
Staff have complained about the suites, and the complaints were quietly set aside.
The distance of the suites may show the executives had lost interest in the floor.
Those imposing the openness exempted themselves, and nobody has objected.

qs.evidence: Meanwhile the executives who commissioned the openness retain their own enclosed suites at the far end of the building, an arrangement nobody has yet described as an obstacle to spontaneous encounter.
qs.answer: Those imposing the openness exempted themselves, and nobody has objected.
qs.why: Kalimatnya menyandingkan pihak yang memerintahkan keterbukaan dengan ruang tertutup yang mereka pertahankan, lalu menutup dengan “nobody has yet described” sebagai penghalang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi urusan rahasia menambahkan pembenaran yang nggak pernah diberikan teks kepada mereka; opsi keluhan yang diabaikan bertabrakan langsung dengan klausa penutup, yang menyebut belum ada yang menyebutnya penghalang; opsi kehilangan minat salah membaca “at the far end”, sebab kata “retain” justru menandakan mereka memegangnya.

qs: What is the writer's tone in describing the silent open-plan floor?
Drily amused at staff who solved the noise by abolishing conversation.
Drily impressed that staff found the one adaptation nobody could forbid them.
Wryly resigned, since silence was always what such a floor would produce.
Dryly comic about a design defeated by the people sitting inside it.

qs.evidence: Employees adapt rationally, acquiring enormous headphones and addressing colleagues exclusively in writing, which produces the pleasant spectacle of an open-plan floor in absolute silence, everybody messaging the neighbour opposite.
qs.answer: Dryly comic about a design defeated by the people sitting inside it.
qs.why: Frasa “the pleasant spectacle” jelas ironis, dan kalimat penutup paragraf itu menyebut arsitekturnya mencapai kebalikan dari tujuan yang diumumkan; jadi leluconnya jatuh pada rancangannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menertawakan staf memindahkan sasaran leluconnya, padahal kata “rationally” justru membela perilaku mereka; opsi kagum pada staf membaca adaptasi itu sebagai kemenangan mereka, bukan kekalahan rancangannya; opsi pasrah bertabrakan dengan “achieved the reverse of its declared purpose”, yang menandai hasil itu sebagai pembalikan, bukan hal yang udah diperkirakan.

qs: In the final paragraph, what are the "neighbourhoods" being sold to companies?
Desk clusters fenced off by partitions and given a friendlier name.
The residential districts that press up against an office building.
Teams grouped by the work they share and seated as one unit.
The informal circles of colleagues who end up sitting near one another.

qs.evidence: We now construct neighbourhoods, quiet pods and zones of intentional focus, which are partitions with superior publicity.
qs.answer: Desk clusters fenced off by partitions and given a friendlier name.
qs.why: Klausa penutup, “which are partitions with superior publicity”, memaksa arti yang bukan arti lazim kata itu: sekat yang dinamai ulang, bukan kawasan tempat tinggal.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi sama presisinya dan masing-masing menamai satu arti sah “neighbourhood”. Opsi kawasan tempat tinggal memakai arti kamus yang paling umum, padahal yang dijual di kalimat ini barang yang dipasang konsultan, “partitions with superior publicity”. Opsi tim yang dikelompokkan menurut pekerjaan menambahkan asas penataan yang nggak pernah disebut. Opsi lingkaran informal menggambarkan “spontaneous encounter” dari paragraf satu, yaitu justru yang dihalangi sekat.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Falling rents are the reason the partitions are now being rebuilt."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Falling rents are the reason the partitions are now being rebuilt.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: I would simply like the record to indicate that the partitions vanished for financial reasons and are reappearing for financial reasons, and that the philosophy has been trailing quietly behind the budget throughout, carrying the bags.
qs.why: Teks memang bilang alasannya keuangan, tapi nggak pernah menyebut sewa turun. Sebab spesifik itu nggak dinyatakan.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” menambah sebab yang nggak ada di teks, dan “False” juga salah karena nggak ada kalimat yang membantah soal sewa.

topic: open-plan offices and the language used to justify them
author: Bagas Wirasena
setting: a critical essay on workplace design

title: Translation Is Loss Arranged Intelligently
text:
A director of considerable reputation announced last spring that dubbing constitutes a form of vandalism, and the internet applauded for roughly a week. Subtitles, we were assured, preserve the performance, while dubbing replaces the actor's soul with a stranger's larynx. It is a stirring argument, delivered with total confidence, and it collapses the moment you examine who is permitted to hold it. Purity is inexpensive when you were raised inside the language the film was shot in.

Consider what subtitles actually cost the viewer, since somebody ought to. Reading occupies the eyes, and the eyes are the instrument the director spent eleven months arranging shots for. Every glance downwards is a small confiscation of the image, and the confiscations accumulate across two hours until a considerable portion of the composition has gone unwatched. The subtitled viewer is not experiencing the film unmediated. That viewer is doing two occupations at once, competently, and calling the result fidelity.

Dubbing, meanwhile, has been unfairly represented by its worst practitioners. Yes, the inexpensive dub arrives with mouths flapping out of sequence and a voice actor apparently reading from a menu. But a translated performance can also be a genuine collaboration, recorded with attention to breath and hesitation, and countries with mature dubbing traditions produce work that their audiences experience as ordinary cinema rather than as damage. My grandmother watched forty years of European films in translation. She could recount their plots more accurately than I manage.

The class dimension is hard to ignore once noticed. Subtitles assume a viewer who reads quickly, sees clearly and was schooled in sustained attention, which characterizes a narrower population than the argument admits. Children, the partially sighted and anyone exhausted after a nine-hour shift are effectively told that the correct way to enjoy world cinema is unavailable to them. The purist position, held sincerely and expressed elegantly, ends up defending an audience of people who resemble the purist.

I watch subtitled films almost exclusively, which is why I am comfortable being rude about the reasoning. My preference is a preference, shaped by education and eyesight, and it acquires no moral weight from being widespread among critics. Let the dub be good, let the subtitles be well timed, and let us abandon the pretence that either route delivers the film untouched. Translation is loss arranged intelligently, and pretending otherwise merely conceals which losses we have chosen to stop noticing.
qs: Read as a whole, what claim about translation does this essay advance?
Every route into a foreign film gives something up, so claiming purity is dishonest.
The purist case is really about class, and it defends an audience like the purist.
Careful dubbing deserves the respect its cheapest examples have cost the practice.
Subtitles confiscate more of the image than the purists have been willing to count.

qs.evidence: Translation is loss arranged intelligently, and pretending otherwise merely conceals which losses we have chosen to stop noticing.
qs.answer: Every route into a foreign film gives something up, so claiming purity is dishonest.
qs.why: Kalimat penutupnya menyebut penerjemahan sebagai kehilangan yang ditata cerdas, dan kalimat sebelumnya meminta dua-duanya baik: “Let the dub be good, let the subtitles be well timed”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh ditulis setegas kunci dan semuanya sejalan dengan tesis esai, tetapi masing-masing hanya satu sisi argumennya. Opsi soal kelas adalah paragraf empat yang dibuka “The class dimension is hard to ignore once noticed”. Opsi membela sulih suara yang cermat dan opsi subtitle yang merampas gambar sama-sama memihak satu jalur, padahal penutupnya menolak peringkat antarjalur, “let the dub be good, let the subtitles be well timed”, dan menuntut kedua kehilangan diakui.

qs: What does the remark about purity being inexpensive imply?
Native speakers may judge a dub more accurately, since they hold the original.
Demanding purity costs nothing if translation was never your problem.
The director's case fails because he had never sat through a good dub.
Purity is a luxury, though only well funded studios can supply it.

qs.evidence: Purity is inexpensive when you were raised inside the language the film was shot in.
qs.answer: Demanding purity costs nothing if translation was never your problem.
qs.why: Kata “inexpensive” di sini soal pengorbanan, bukan uang: kalau filmnya udah dalam bahasamu, menuntut kemurnian nggak menuntut apa pun darimu.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi penutur asli menilai lebih akurat menambahkan keunggulan penilaian yang nggak diklaim teks, sebab yang dipersoalkan siapa yang berhak memegang argumennya; opsi sutradara belum pernah menonton sulih suara bagus menambahkan riwayat yang nggak ada; opsi studio kaya membaca “inexpensive” sebagai biaya produksi, padahal kalimatnya bicara tentang penontonnya.

qs: What does the writer achieve by describing the cheap dub in this way?
He concedes the weakest case with a joke, then goes on defending the practice.
He hands the purists their best example and leaves it standing unanswered.
He mocks cheap dubbing hard enough to keep his own taste above suspicion.
He treats bad dubbing as a funding problem the industry could fix tomorrow.

qs.evidence: Yes, the inexpensive dub arrives with mouths flapping out of sequence and a voice actor apparently reading from a menu.
qs.answer: He concedes the weakest case with a joke, then goes on defending the practice.
qs.why: Kalimat itu dibuka “Yes”, yaitu pengakuan, dan disampaikan sebagai lelucon; kalimat berikutnya dibuka “But a translated performance can also be a genuine collaboration”, jadi konsesinya melayani pembelaan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi dibiarkan tanpa jawaban bertabrakan dengan kata “But” di kalimat berikutnya; opsi menjaga seleranya sendiri memindahkan pengakuan paragraf lima tentang kebiasaan menontonnya ke tempat ini; opsi soal pendanaan menambahkan tuntutan anggaran yang nggak pernah diajukan teks.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the point about glancing downwards?
A glance down costs little, since the eye returns before the shot has moved.
Subtitles sit low enough to leave the composition of the shot intact.
The loss is real, but a viewer stops noticing it, which comes to the same thing.
Reading the lines steadily removes parts of the picture you never get to see.

qs.evidence: Every glance downwards is a small confiscation of the image, and the confiscations accumulate across two hours until a considerable portion of the composition has gone unwatched.
qs.answer: Reading the lines steadily removes parts of the picture you never get to see.
qs.why: Setiap tundukan mata disebut penyitaan kecil, dan penyitaan itu menumpuk sampai sebagian besar komposisinya nggak tertonton.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi biayanya kecil membalik kata “accumulate”; opsi komposisi tetap utuh bertabrakan dengan “gone unwatched”; opsi berhenti menyadarinya memakai kalimat penutup esai tentang kehilangan yang tak lagi kita sadari, padahal kalimat ini menyatakan bagiannya benar-benar hilang, disadari atau nggak.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "The writer prefers dubbed versions for his own viewing."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: The writer prefers dubbed versions for his own viewing.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: I watch subtitled films almost exclusively, which is why I am comfortable being rude about the reasoning.
qs.why: Dia menonton hampir selalu dengan subtitle, jadi klaim ini bertentangan langsung dengan kebiasaannya.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertabrakan dengan kata “almost exclusively”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena preferensinya disebut jelas.

topic: the argument between subtitles and dubbing
author: Fajar Melanto
setting: a critical essay on film translation

title: Spilling the Beans at Five
text:
Children learn idioms rather later than the surrounding vocabulary, and the delay has proved unexpectedly informative for developmental linguistics. A five-year-old who handles several thousand words competently will nevertheless interpret spill the beans as an accident involving a saucepan. The literal reading is not a deficiency of intelligence. It is the sensible output of a system rewarded thousands of times for assuming that sentences mean the sum of their parts. Figurative competence requires the child to suspend that assumption selectively, which is a much harder operation.

Comprehension studies conducted with primary pupils suggest three factors govern the timing. Familiarity matters most, since frequently encountered expressions are acquired almost as single vocabulary items long before their internal logic is understood. Transparency matters next: an idiom whose literal image resembles its meaning, such as holding the reins, yields earlier than an opaque one like kicking the bucket. Context supplies the remainder, and children perform clearly better when an expression arrives inside a narrative that supports only one plausible interpretation.

The developmental sequence appears to run through a stage that researchers have described, perhaps too neatly, as productive error. Around the age of seven many children begin generating idioms of their own, announcing that a difficult classmate has lost his batteries or that a dull afternoon tasted of paper. These inventions are frequently dismissed as charming mistakes by adults, yet they demonstrate that the underlying mechanism has been grasped. The child has understood that language permits systematic borrowing between domains, and is now practising the borrowing without institutional approval.

Instructional implications follow, though cautiously. Explicit teaching of idiom lists produces reliable gains on recognition tests and disappointing gains on production, a pattern familiar from other areas of vocabulary work. Programmes that embed expressions inside repeated narrative, and that invite pupils to invent parallel figures, appear to transfer more reliably. One classroom study in a bilingual primary school reported that pupils who had invented their own metaphors retained the taught idioms considerably better nine weeks afterwards. The sample was small, however, and the effect has not yet been replicated elsewhere.

The wider point concerns what we count as linguistic knowledge. A learner who defines an idiom correctly on a written test may still fail to notice when a colleague deploys it ironically. Irony detection develops later still, extending well into adolescence. Figurative language is therefore best understood not as an ornamental layer added to a completed grammar, but as a slow negotiation between what sentences say and what speakers are doing with them. The negotiation is never entirely finished, in children or in the rest of us.
qs: Read as a whole, what conclusion does this article reach about idioms in childhood?
Idiom learning is governed largely by familiarity, transparency and context.
Inventing metaphors may teach idiom better than learning lists of them does.
Literal reading is the sensible output of a well trained system, not a failure.
Idiom belongs to learning what speakers do with language, not to decorating grammar.

qs.evidence: Figurative language is therefore best understood not as an ornamental layer added to a completed grammar, but as a slow negotiation between what sentences say and what speakers are doing with them.
qs.answer: Idiom belongs to learning what speakers do with language, not to decorating grammar.
qs.why: Paragraf terakhir dibuka “The wider point concerns what we count as linguistic knowledge”, lalu kalimat ini merumuskan kesimpulannya dengan pasangan “not as … but as …”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tiga faktor adalah temuan paragraf dua yang dipakai menjelaskan waktu penguasaan, bukan kesimpulan artikelnya; opsi mengarang kiasan adalah implikasi pengajaran di paragraf empat, yang teks sendiri beri catatan “The sample was small, however”; opsi pembacaan harfiah adalah pengamatan pembuka yang menyiapkan argumennya.

qs: What do the invented expressions at around seven years old suggest?
Children of seven reproduce the idioms they hear at home before inventing any.
Children reach for figurative language before anybody has taught it to them.
The inventions are charming mistakes, and adults dismiss them before looking closer.
Children copy the pattern of idioms they have met often enough to imitate.

qs.evidence: Around the age of seven many children begin generating idioms of their own, announcing that a difficult classmate has lost his batteries or that a dull afternoon tasted of paper.
qs.answer: Children reach for figurative language before anybody has taught it to them.
qs.why: Kata “generating … of their own” dan contoh yang nggak ada dalam idiom mana pun menunjukkan anak memakai kiasan tanpa lebih dulu diajari.
qs.whyOthersFail: Dua pengecoh memakai penanda “before” yang sama dengan kunci, jadi bentuk itu nggak lagi menunjuk jawaban. Opsi mengulang idiom rumah bertabrakan dengan kata “generating” dan dengan kedua contohnya, yang bukan idiom yang beredar. Opsi kekeliruan menggemaskan mengambil penilaian orang dewasa yang justru dibantah klausa berikutnya, “yet they demonstrate that the underlying mechanism has been grasped”. Opsi meniru pola memakai faktor familiarity dari paragraf dua, padahal yang ditunjukkan di sini peminjaman antarranah tanpa contoh untuk ditiru.

qs: What does the aside about the researchers' label reveal about the writer's stance?
A mild reserve towards a label that may have tidied the evidence up.
Quiet approval of a label that names the stage more economically than prose could.
A gentle joke, perhaps, at researchers naming a stage after its errors.
Faint impatience with a sequence that may still rest on one classroom study.

qs.evidence: The developmental sequence appears to run through a stage that researchers have described, perhaps too neatly, as productive error.
qs.answer: A mild reserve towards a label that may have tidied the evidence up.
qs.why: Sisipan “perhaps too neatly” menyasar kerapian istilahnya, dan kata “perhaps” menjaganya tetap sebagai keberatan kecil, bukan penolakan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi persetujuan mengabaikan sisipan “perhaps too neatly”, yang jelas menahan diri; opsi lelucon soal penamaan menyasar pilihan katanya, padahal keberatannya soal kerapian yang berlebihan, bukan istilah yang diambil dari kekeliruan; opsi nggak sabar memindahkan catatan sampel kecil dari paragraf empat ke istilah ini, dan melampaui kata “perhaps”.

qs: In the second paragraph, what does "Transparency" refer to?
How openly a teacher explains where an expression originally came from.
How clearly the surrounding story points towards one available reading.
How closely the picture inside an expression matches what it means.
How often pupils meet the expression in ordinary classroom speech.

qs.evidence: Transparency matters next: an idiom whose literal image resembles its meaning, such as holding the reins, yields earlier than an opaque one like kicking the bucket.
qs.answer: How closely the picture inside an expression matches what it means.
qs.why: Definisinya diberikan di kalimat itu sendiri, dan pasangan contohnya memaksa arti teknis, bukan arti lazim kata itu sebagai keterbukaan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi guru menjelaskan asal usul memakai arti kamus yang paling umum, yaitu keterbukaan, padahal yang diukur di sini sifat idiomnya; opsi cerita di sekelilingnya adalah faktor konteks di kalimat sesudahnya; opsi seberapa sering adalah familiarity di kalimat sebelumnya.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Noticing an ironic use of an idiom develops after the ability to define it."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Noticing an ironic use of an idiom develops after the ability to define it.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: Irony detection develops later still, extending well into adolescence.
qs.why: Teks menaruh deteksi ironi setelah kemampuan mendefinisikan, dan bilang itu berlanjut sampai remaja.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan kata “later still”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena urutannya disebut jelas.

topic: how children come to understand idioms and figurative language
author: Dr Lestari Handayani
setting: an academic article on language development

title: A Story About Pens
text:
The claim that handwritten notes produce deeper learning than typed ones has travelled far beyond the evidence supporting it, which is itself a mildly interesting phenomenon. The original finding was modest and specific: students who wrote by hand recorded fewer words, paraphrased more, and performed better on questions requiring conceptual integration. Nothing in that result concerned ink, paper, or the general romance of stationery. The mechanism proposed was slowness, and slowness happens to be the one variable that popular retellings almost invariably omit.

Subsequent replications have complicated the picture considerably. Several studies found no reliable advantage once note quality was controlled statistically, and one large sample reported an advantage for typing among students who had been taught a summarizing strategy beforehand. The pattern that survives across the whole literature is not a contest between instruments. It is a contest between transcription and reformulation, which either instrument can support and either instrument can obstruct depending on how the student has been trained.

Transcription is attractive precisely because it feels so productive at the time. A verbatim record offers reassurance, it demands no decisions during the lecture, and it postpones the discomfort of discovering that a passage was never understood. Reformulation reverses each of those properties, which explains its unpopularity among students under examination pressure. The handwriting condition in the original experiments effectively imposed reformulation by physical means, since nobody can write quickly enough to transcribe a lecturer speaking at ordinary speed.

Two practical consequences deserve mention. First, interventions that teach reformulation directly appear to reduce the instrument effect towards insignificance, which suggests the instrument was never the active ingredient. Second, prohibiting laptops in lecture theatres, a policy several departments adopted enthusiastically after the initial publicity, may impose genuine costs. Students who type because handwriting is painful or slow for them lose an accommodation, while the promised benefits could be supplied by better teaching instead.

The episode illustrates a recurring hazard in educational research, and the hazard is not fraud. A carefully bounded finding acquires a memorable narrative, the narrative circulates faster than its qualifications, and the qualifications eventually arrive to an audience that has already redesigned its policies. Researchers bear some responsibility for the compression, since a paper titled after its mechanism rather than its instruments would have travelled differently. Readers bear the rest, for preferring a story about pens to a story about cognitive effort, which is admittedly the less charming of the two.
qs: How does the writer relate the choice of instrument to the quality of notes?
The instrument decides the outcome, whatever training the student has had.
Slowness is the pen's own gift, so handwriting keeps a modest advantage.
Training matters, but only once the student has settled on an instrument.
The tool matters less than whether the student rewords or merely copies.

qs.evidence: It is a contest between transcription and reformulation, which either instrument can support and either instrument can obstruct depending on how the student has been trained.
qs.answer: The tool matters less than whether the student rewords or merely copies.
qs.why: Kalimat itu memindahkan pertandingannya dari alat ke perilaku, dan menyebut kedua alat bisa mendukung ataupun menghalangi keduanya, tergantung latihan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi alat menentukan justru yang dibatalkan klausa “either instrument can support and either instrument can obstruct”; opsi keunggulan pena memakai mekanisme kelambatan dari paragraf tiga, tetapi kalimat ini menyebut kelambatan hanya cara memaksa perumusan ulang, bukan keunggulan alatnya; opsi latihan menyusul pilihan alat menukar urutan sebabnya, sebab teks menempatkan latihan sebagai penentu.

qs: What can be inferred about why handwriting appeared to help in the original study?
The physical act of writing fixed the material in memory more firmly.
Its slowness forced those students to condense what they were hearing.
Those students had been taught a summarizing strategy before the lecture.
Recording fewer words left them free to follow the lecturer's argument.

qs.evidence: The handwriting condition in the original experiments effectively imposed reformulation by physical means, since nobody can write quickly enough to transcribe a lecturer speaking at ordinary speed.
qs.answer: Its slowness forced those students to condense what they were hearing.
qs.why: Klausa sebabnya menyebut nggak ada yang bisa menulis secepat dosen berbicara, jadi kecepatan tangan itulah yang memaksa pemadatan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh menyebut mekanisme yang sama tegasnya dengan kunci. Opsi tangan dan ingatan adalah penjelasan populer yang ditolak paragraf satu, “Nothing in that result concerned ink, paper, or the general romance of stationery”. Opsi latihan meringkas memindahkan syarat itu ke kelompok yang salah, sebab teks melekatkannya pada sampel besar yang berpihak pada papan tombol. Opsi sedikit kata membalik arah sebabnya, karena jumlah kata yang sedikit adalah akibat kecepatan tulis, bukan sebabnya.

qs: What attitude does the closing sentence take towards readers?
Wryly forgiving, though granting that the duller account never wins an audience.
Drily even-handed, while splitting the blame without weighting either half.
Sharply reproachful, laying the whole failure at the audience's door.
Gently critical, while granting that the duller account is harder to like.

qs.evidence: Readers bear the rest, for preferring a story about pens to a story about cognitive effort, which is admittedly the less charming of the two.
qs.answer: Gently critical, while granting that the duller account is harder to like.
qs.why: Kalimatnya melakukan dua hal: menaruh sisa tanggung jawab pada pembaca, lalu mengakui versi yang benar memang kurang menarik. Kritiknya ada, tetapi ditahan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi memaafkan menghapus klausa “Readers bear the rest”, yang jelas menuntut; opsi berbagi rata bertabrakan dengan pembagiannya, sebab peneliti hanya diberi “some responsibility” sedangkan pembaca menanggung sisanya; opsi teguran keras mengabaikan kata “admittedly”, yang justru membenarkan sebagian pilihan pembaca.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the account of how findings travel?
The limits travel with the finding, and the policy is what lags behind.
The small print catches up first, and the policies are revised before anyone acts.
The catchy version outruns the small print and arrives after people have acted.
The finding is simplified by its authors, and the story arrives already shortened.

qs.evidence: A carefully bounded finding acquires a memorable narrative, the narrative circulates faster than its qualifications, and the qualifications eventually arrive to an audience that has already redesigned its policies.
qs.answer: The catchy version outruns the small print and arrives after people have acted.
qs.why: Kalimat itu menyusun tiga tahap: narasi yang mudah diingat, peredaran yang lebih cepat daripada syaratnya, lalu syarat yang datang setelah kebijakan dirombak.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi memakai rangka dua-bagian yang sama, sehingga nggak ada satu pun yang lebih elegan. Opsi batasan yang ikut beredar membalik klausa tengahnya, “circulates faster than its qualifications”. Opsi syarat yang menyusul lebih dulu bertabrakan dengan “already redesigned its policies”. Opsi penyederhanaan sebagai kerja penulis memindahkan pelakunya, sebab tanggung jawab peneliti baru dibahas di kalimat sesudahnya, sementara kalimat ini menerangkan urutan dan kecepatan.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Every later replication confirmed the original advantage for writing by hand."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Every later replication confirmed the original advantage for writing by hand.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Several studies found no reliable advantage once note quality was controlled statistically, and one large sample reported an advantage for typing among students who had been taught a summarizing strategy beforehand.
qs.why: Beberapa studi nggak menemukan keunggulan itu dan satu sampel besar justru berpihak pada papan tombol. Klaim ini bertentangan.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertabrakan dengan hasil replikasi tersebut, dan “Not stated” gagal karena hasilnya dilaporkan di paragraf dua.

topic: research on handwritten versus typed lecture notes
author: Dr Anwar Sulaiman
setting: an academic article on note-taking research

title: No Rush At All
text:
Workplace email occupies an awkward position between the memorandum and the conversation, and its politeness markers have accordingly become peculiar, a peculiarity worth documenting. A corpus of eleven thousand internal messages, collected from three organizations over two years, shows that the commonest softening device is not please but a temporal hedge. Writers postpone their demand behind expressions such as when you get a moment, no rush at all, or whenever convenient. The demand then arrives with a deadline attached two lines later, unhedged and unmistakable.

The salient property of these hedges is that recipients decode them accurately and resent them anyway. In follow-up interviews, participants described no rush as meaning today, and described just checking in as meaning you are late. This is not misunderstanding; the pragmatic content transmits perfectly, and what the hedge accomplishes instead is deniability. The sender may afterwards insist that no pressure was applied at all, since the surface text plainly says otherwise.

Frequency data reveal a hierarchy that nobody inside the three organizations ever described openly, nor indeed acknowledged privately. Hedging increases sharply when a writer addresses somebody senior, which is unsurprising, but it also increases when a writer addresses somebody in a separate department at an equivalent grade. Messages travelling downwards contain the fewest hedges and the highest proportion of bare imperatives. Politeness in this corpus therefore tracks the absence of authority rather than the presence of respect, a distinction that the everyday word politeness obscures rather badly.

Two further patterns merit comment, both distinctly unflattering. The exclamation mark functions as a class of its own, appearing four times more frequently in refusals than in messages granting a request. The extra cheerfulness apparently compensates for the disappointment it manufactures. Meanwhile apologies cluster at the outset of messages sent outside working hours, where they operate less as regret than as an announcement that the sender is virtuous, hardworking and awake at eleven.

None of this indicts anybody in particular, and senior staff hedge downwards only when a request is genuinely optional, which happens seldom. Hedged demands are a rational adaptation to a channel that preserves everything in writing and circulates it beyond the intended reader. A blunt instruction may be forwarded to a manager without further comment; a softened one presumably will not be. The corpus consequently documents an environment in which individuals write defensively, permanently, because the medium remembers and forwards. The politest sentence in the collection, offered without irony by a project lead, reads: happy to discuss whenever suits you, though I will need this before lunch.
qs: How does the corpus relate hedging to a writer's place in the hierarchy?
Hedging increases as the writer's respect for the reader increases.
Hedging stays level across the grades, and only the wording changes.
Hedging increases as the writer's authority over the reader increases.
Hedging increases as the writer's authority over the reader decreases.

qs.evidence: Politeness in this corpus therefore tracks the absence of authority rather than the presence of respect, a distinction that the everyday word politeness obscures rather badly.
qs.answer: Hedging increases as the writer's authority over the reader decreases.
qs.why: Teks menyimpulkan kesopanan dalam korpus ini mengikuti ketiadaan wewenang, bukan kehadiran rasa hormat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi memakai rangka “Hedging increases as X” yang sama, jadi nggak ada satu pun yang lebih presisi. Opsi rasa hormat persis yang dipisahkan kalimat penutup paragraf tiga, “tracks the absence of authority rather than the presence of respect”. Opsi sebaran yang merata bertabrakan dengan “increases sharply” di kalimat sebelumnya. Opsi wewenang yang justru naik membalik “Messages travelling downwards contain the fewest hedges”.

qs: What can be inferred about why writers prefer these temporal hedges?
The wording may keep recipients from working out when a task is really due.
The wording reflects a real wish, though a modest one, to leave some room.
The wording is copied from senior colleagues, since juniors imitate what arrives.
The wording gives the sender a defence if the pressure is later challenged.

qs.evidence: The sender may afterwards insist that no pressure was applied at all, since the surface text plainly says otherwise.
qs.answer: The wording gives the sender a defence if the pressure is later challenged.
qs.why: Kalimat itu menyebut gunanya bagi pengirim: teks permukaannya bisa dipakai untuk bersikeras bahwa nggak ada tekanan yang pernah diberikan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi menyembunyikan tenggat bertabrakan dengan “recipients decode them accurately” dan dengan tenggat yang muncul dua baris kemudian; opsi keinginan tulus ditolak kalimat “what the hedge accomplishes instead is deniability”; opsi meniru atasan menambahkan jalur penularan yang nggak pernah disebut korpusnya.

qs: What is the effect of ending the article with the quoted message?
It lets one example carry the whole finding, and leaves the joke to the reader.
It shows the writer partly admires a sentence that manages both jobs at once.
It quietly excuses the senders, since the deadline at least appears in plain words.
It hands the pattern back as a puzzle the article may have decided not to solve.

qs.evidence: The politest sentence in the collection, offered without irony by a project lead, reads: happy to discuss whenever suits you, though I will need this before lunch.
qs.answer: It lets one example carry the whole finding, and leaves the joke to the reader.
qs.why: Kalimat itu disebut yang paling sopan dalam koleksi, lalu ternyata memuat tenggat sebelum makan siang; satu contoh merangkum temuan tanpa perlu komentar tambahan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi mengagumi kalimatnya menambahkan penilaian estetis yang nggak ada, sebab kutipan itu diberi kerangka “The politest sentence in the collection, offered without irony”; opsi memaafkan pengirim bertabrakan dengan paragraf dua yang menyebut pengirim memakai deniability; opsi teka-teki yang tak dipecahkan bertabrakan dengan artikel yang udah menyatakan temuannya di paragraf tiga.

qs: In the third paragraph, what does "an equivalent grade" mean?
The same rank in the organization, though in another department.
The same mark, though awarded for work the two of them had shared.
A comparable level of politeness, though measured across the whole corpus.
The same length of service, whatever job title either of them holds.

qs.evidence: Hedging increases sharply when a writer addresses somebody senior, which is unsurprising, but it also increases when a writer addresses somebody in a separate department at an equivalent grade.
qs.answer: The same rank in the organization, though in another department.
qs.why: Kalimat itu memasang porosnya lewat kata “somebody senior”, lalu frasa ini menandai lawannya: setara wewenang tetapi beda departemen, bukan arti lazim kata itu sebagai nilai ujian.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi nilai tugas memakai arti kamus “grade” yang paling umum, padahal kalimat ini membandingkan posisi dalam organisasi; opsi tingkat kesopanan memindahkan variabel yang diukur menjadi hasilnya; opsi lama masa kerja menambahkan ukuran yang nggak disebut, sebab kalimatnya memasangkan “equivalent grade” dengan “somebody senior”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Exclamation marks appear more often in messages from senior staff than from junior staff."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Exclamation marks appear more often in messages from senior staff than from junior staff.
qs.answer: Not stated
qs.evidence: The exclamation mark functions as a class of its own, appearing four times more frequently in refusals than in messages granting a request.
qs.why: Teks hanya membandingkan penolakan dengan persetujuan. Perbandingan antar jenjang jabatan nggak pernah dibuat.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” dan “False” butuh angka per jenjang yang nggak ada; kalimat terdekat membandingkan hal yang berbeda.

author: Dr Wulan Perdani
setting: an academic article on corpus linguistics

title: Tension Is Not Ugliness
text:
Musical dissonance is routinely described as unpleasant, and the description survives despite a century of evidence that it depends heavily on what a listener has previously heard. The physical account is elegant and incomplete. Two tones whose frequencies sit close together produce a roughness in the ear that most listeners report as tension. The effect can be measured in populations who have never received formal training. It does not follow that the tension is experienced as ugly, and the difference between tension and ugliness carries most of the argument.

A listening experiment conducted with two hundred adults illustrates the distinction. Participants rated chords for pleasantness after four weeks of daily exposure to unfamiliar harmonic material, one group hearing dense chords in a narrative film context, the other hearing identical chords in isolation. Both groups showed increased tolerance, but only the film group reported enjoyment. The chord had not changed. What had changed was the listener's sense of what the chord was for, which suggests that meaning arrives before comfort rather than after it.

Historical evidence points in a similar direction, if less tidily. Intervals now taught to beginners as consonant were once formally prohibited in liturgical composition, and audiences in several documented cases laughed at works whose harmonic language later became a standard examination text. Retrospective accounts of these episodes tend to praise the composer and patronize the audience. A less flattering reading is available: the audience heard accurately, and simply lacked the twenty years of subsequent listening that made the material legible.

The pedagogical consequence is uncomfortable for curriculum designers. If tolerance grows through exposure embedded in meaningful context, then teaching harmony as a set of rules about permitted intervals inverts the actual developmental order. Pupils would presumably acquire more if the strange chord arrived attached to a story, a film sequence or a physical gesture, with the theoretical vocabulary supplied afterwards. Several conservatories have experimented along these lines, and the reported results are encouraging without yet being conclusive.

There remains a residual puzzle that the exposure account does not dissolve. Certain combinations continue to be rated as distressing by trained listeners who have encountered them for decades and who can explain their function fluently. Familiarity has not domesticated them, which implies a floor beneath which acculturation does not reach. Where exactly that floor lies is unresolved, and the honest position is that we know considerably more about why dissonance becomes acceptable than about why a stubborn residue never does.
qs: Read as a whole, what does this article contend about tension in music?
Meaning arrives before comfort, which is largely why context does the teaching.
Rough chords create tension, and tension is not the same thing as ugliness.
Harmony should be taught through story and gesture before any rules are named.
A stubborn residue resists exposure, though nobody knows quite why it does.

qs.evidence: It does not follow that the tension is experienced as ugly, and the difference between tension and ugliness carries most of the argument.
qs.answer: Rough chords create tension, and tension is not the same thing as ugliness.
qs.why: Kalimat itu menunjuk dirinya sendiri sebagai pokok: pembedaan antara ketegangan dan keburukan disebut memikul sebagian besar argumennya.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi makna sebelum kenyamanan adalah kesimpulan eksperimen paragraf dua, satu langkah di dalam argumennya; opsi cara mengajar adalah implikasi pedagogis paragraf empat, yang teks sebut “encouraging without yet being conclusive”; opsi sisa yang membandel adalah teka-teki sisa di paragraf lima, dibuka “There remains a residual puzzle”.

qs: What does the outcome of the four-week listening experiment suggest?
Tolerance depends on the context in which the chords were heard.
Enjoyment depends on how many weeks of daily exposure a listener gets.
Enjoyment depends on the story pulling attention away from the chord.
Enjoyment depends on the purpose a listener can attach to a sound.

qs.evidence: Both groups showed increased tolerance, but only the film group reported enjoyment.
qs.answer: Enjoyment depends on the purpose a listener can attach to a sound.
qs.why: Toleransi naik di kedua kelompok dan akordnya nggak berubah, jadi yang membedakan kenikmatan hanyalah kegunaan yang bisa dibayangkan pendengar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi memakai rangka “depends on” yang sama dan sama tegasnya. Opsi toleransi yang bergantung konteks bertabrakan dengan “Both groups showed increased tolerance”. Opsi jumlah minggu paparan menghapus satu-satunya pembeda antarkelompok, sebab keduanya mendapat empat minggu yang sama. Opsi perhatian yang teralih menambahkan mekanisme lain, padahal teks menamai mekanismenya, “the listener's sense of what the chord was for”.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards the retrospective accounts of those episodes?
Sceptical of the audiences, since they laughed at what later became a set examination text.
Detached, since the record of those episodes is too thin to weigh either way.
Sceptical of the accounts, since they flatter the composer at the audience's cost.
Amused by accounts that at least kept the laughter in the historical record.

qs.evidence: Retrospective accounts of these episodes tend to praise the composer and patronize the audience.
qs.answer: Sceptical of the accounts, since they flatter the composer at the audience's cost.
qs.why: Kata “patronize” adalah penilaian penulis atas catatan belakangan itu, dan kalimat berikutnya menawarkan “a less flattering reading” yang membela pendengar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh sejalan dengan tesis akulturasi dan sama tegasnya dengan kunci, tetapi salah sasaran atau salah derajat. Opsi meragukan penonton menyasar pihak yang salah, sebab kalimat berikutnya menyebut “the audience heard accurately”. Opsi berjarak mengabaikan kata “patronize”, yang jelas menilai. Opsi terhibur menambahkan penghargaan pada catatan itu yang nggak ada di teks.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the point about a floor in the final paragraph?
Some sounds stay disturbing however long a listener lives with them.
Some sounds grow comfortable however strange they seemed at the start.
Some sounds mark where acculturation begins, however far it later reaches.
Trained listeners stop minding such sounds, however distressing they once were.

qs.evidence: Familiarity has not domesticated them, which implies a floor beneath which acculturation does not reach.
qs.answer: Some sounds stay disturbing however long a listener lives with them.
qs.why: Frasa “a floor beneath which acculturation does not reach” menandai batas bawah: keakraban nggak menjinakkan kombinasi tertentu, berapa lama pun didengar.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi memakai rangka konsesif “however” yang sama, sehingga bentuknya sama-sama rapi. Opsi bunyi yang akhirnya melunak persis yang dibatasi “Familiarity has not domesticated them”. Opsi lantai sebagai titik awal membalik kiasannya, sebab “a floor beneath which acculturation does not reach” adalah batas bawah. Opsi pendengar terlatih yang berhenti terganggu bertabrakan dengan “continue to be rated as distressing by trained listeners”.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Listeners with no formal training can also register the roughness of close tones."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Listeners with no formal training can also register the roughness of close tones.
qs.answer: True
qs.evidence: The effect can be measured in populations who have never received formal training.
qs.why: Efek itu terukur pada orang yang belum pernah dilatih, jadi klaimnya parafrasa yang benar.
qs.whyOthersFail: “False” bertentangan dengan kalimat itu, dan “Not stated” gagal karena datanya disebut di paragraf pertama.

topic: why listeners come to accept musical dissonance
author: Dr Bening Larasati
setting: an academic article on music perception

title: Two Kinds of Variety
text:
Recommendation systems are commonly accused of narrowing taste, and the accusation is popular partly because it is easy to picture. The listener is imagined descending a tunnel, each selection slightly more similar to the last, until the whole musical world has contracted to a single mood. Measurement complicates that picture considerably without entirely refuting it. Aggregate consumption on the platforms studied has become more diverse by several standard metrics, while individual consumption has frequently become less so, and both statements describe the same population.

The apparent contradiction resolves once diversity is defined carefully. Catalogue diversity counts how many distinct works receive attention across all users. The figure rises when a system surfaces obscure material to the small audiences likely to accept it. Individual diversity counts how far a single listener travels within a period, and this figure falls when the system successfully predicts preference. A platform can therefore expand the collective repertoire while confining each subscriber to a comfortable corner of it, and marketing departments may honestly cite whichever number flatters the product.

Longitudinal data introduce a further wrinkle concerning the direction of causation. Listeners whose diversity declined most sharply after adopting algorithmic playlists were, in one analysis of three years of logs, already among the least exploratory beforehand. The system amplified an existing disposition rather than creating it, which is a weaker claim than the tunnel metaphor implies and a more difficult one to legislate against. Regulation designed for a machine that manufactures narrowness will miss a machine that merely rewards it.

Interventions have nevertheless been tested, with mixed and instructive outcomes. Inserting deliberately unfamiliar items at a low rate increases exploration modestly and reduces satisfaction scores immediately, which explains why few commercial systems retain the feature after trialling it. Explanations perform better than surprises: telling a listener why an item was chosen raises willingness to accept the unexpected. An unexplained recommendation feels like an error, whereas an explained one feels like an invitation.

The broader lesson concerns what these systems are optimizing, and they are not optimizing for the listener a critic has in mind. They are optimizing for continuation, a measurable proxy that correlates with satisfaction in the short term and with something closer to sedation over longer intervals. Nobody in the industry ever chose sedation. It emerged from a reasonable objective, pursued diligently, in the absence of any metric capable of noticing the difference between contentment and mild anaesthesia.
qs: How are the two kinds of diversity related on these platforms?
The shared catalogue can widen while each listener's range widens with it.
The shared catalogue can widen while each listener's own range narrows.
Each listener's range can widen while the shared catalogue quietly narrows.
The shared catalogue can narrow while each listener's range stays where it was.

qs.evidence: A platform can therefore expand the collective repertoire while confining each subscriber to a comfortable corner of it, and marketing departments may honestly cite whichever number flatters the product.
qs.answer: The shared catalogue can widen while each listener's own range narrows.
qs.why: Kalimat itu menyatakan kedua angka bisa bergerak berlawanan pada populasi yang sama, dan justru itu yang membuat bagian pemasaran bisa memilih angka yang menyanjung.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi berbentuk paradoks dua-arah yang sama rapinya, jadi bentuknya nggak lagi menunjuk kunci. Opsi kedua ukuran melebar bersama bertabrakan dengan kalimat yang menyebut ukuran individu justru turun ketika ramalan berhasil, “this figure falls when the system successfully predicts preference”. Opsi arah terbalik menukar kedua ukuran itu. Opsi katalog yang menyempit bertabrakan dengan paragraf satu, “Aggregate consumption on the platforms studied has become more diverse”.

qs: A platform trials the insertion of unfamiliar tracks at a low rate. What sequence do the tested interventions predict?
Exploration rises modestly, satisfaction scores fall at once, and the feature is withdrawn.
Exploration rises sharply, and satisfaction climbs after a delay of some weeks.
Exploration stays flat, so the feature survives as a harmless piece of decoration.
Exploration rises and the feature is kept, because a reason accompanies each insertion.

qs.evidence: Inserting deliberately unfamiliar items at a low rate increases exploration modestly and reduces satisfaction scores immediately, which explains why few commercial systems retain the feature after trialling it.
qs.answer: Exploration rises modestly, satisfaction scores fall at once, and the feature is withdrawn.
qs.why: Paragraf empat melaporkan urutan itu sebagai hasil uji: penyisipan lagu asing menaikkan eksplorasi sedikit, menurunkan skor kepuasan seketika, dan karena itu “few commercial systems retain the feature after trialling it”.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi eksplorasi naik tajam salah pada dua angka sekaligus: kenaikannya “modestly”, dan kepuasan turun segera, bukan naik terlambat. Opsi eksplorasi datar bertabrakan langsung dengan kenaikan yang dilaporkan. Opsi fitur dipertahankan karena setiap sisipan diberi alasan menggabungkan dua temuan berbeda: teks memang bilang penjelasan menaikkan penerimaan hal tak terduga, tetapi nggak pernah bilang fitur penyisipan itu dipertahankan — yang tercatat justru sebaliknya.

qs: What does the writer imply by describing the long-term result as sedation?
That continuation, pursued far enough, dulls a listener rather than pleasing one.
That the industry preferred a dulled listener to one who might leave the service.
That the word overstates the case rather than naming what actually happens.
That satisfaction and continuation are the same thing measured twice over.

qs.evidence: They are optimizing for continuation, a measurable proxy that correlates with satisfaction in the short term and with something closer to sedation over longer intervals.
qs.answer: That continuation, pursued far enough, dulls a listener rather than pleasing one.
qs.why: Kalimat itu memasang dua rentang waktu pada satu ukuran: kepuasan dalam jangka pendek, sesuatu yang lebih dekat ke sedasi dalam jangka panjang.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh sejalan dengan tesis bahwa sistem dioptimalkan untuk kelanjutan, tetapi masing-masing salah pada satu sinyal. Opsi industri yang lebih suka pendengar tumpul bertabrakan dengan “Nobody in the industry ever chose sedation”. Opsi kata yang dilebih-lebihkan mengabaikan kalimat penutup, yang menyebut tak ada ukuran yang mampu membedakan kepuasan dari anestesi ringan. Opsi kepuasan sama dengan kelanjutan hanya memakai separuh kalimatnya, “correlates with satisfaction in the short term”.

qs: Which statement comes closest in meaning to the closing point of the fourth paragraph?
A suggestion lands much the same, though a reason may come with it.
Explaining a choice makes a listener suspect the system has slipped up.
Give a reason and an odd suggestion reads as an offer, not a fault.
Surprises may work better than reasons, provided they arrive at a low rate.

qs.evidence: An unexplained recommendation feels like an error, whereas an explained one feels like an invitation.
qs.answer: Give a reason and an odd suggestion reads as an offer, not a fault.
qs.why: Kalimat itu memasangkan dua rasa: tanpa penjelasan terasa keliru, dengan penjelasan terasa seperti tawaran.
qs.whyOthersFail: Opsi tanpa beda bertabrakan dengan “Explanations perform better than surprises”; opsi penjelasan menimbulkan curiga membalik kalimat penutupnya, sebab yang terasa keliru adalah rekomendasi tanpa penjelasan; opsi kejutan lebih unggul membalik peringkat yang dinyatakan paragraf itu.

qs: Is this statement true, false, or not stated? — "Most commercial systems have kept the feature that inserts unfamiliar items."
True
False
Not stated

qs.claim: Most commercial systems have kept the feature that inserts unfamiliar items.
qs.answer: False
qs.evidence: Inserting deliberately unfamiliar items at a low rate increases exploration modestly and reduces satisfaction scores immediately, which explains why few commercial systems retain the feature after trialling it.
qs.why: Teks bilang hanya sedikit sistem komersial yang mempertahankan fitur itu, jadi klaim ini bertolak belakang.
qs.whyOthersFail: “True” bertentangan dengan kata “few”, dan “Not stated” gagal karena nasib fitur itu dilaporkan.

topic: how recommendation systems affect the diversity of listening
author: Dr Iqbal Nurhadi
setting: an academic article on algorithmic recommendation

title: Going Beautifully
text:
Irony presents an unusual problem for models of comprehension, because the listener must reject the sentence that was actually uttered. When a colleague surveys a collapsed schedule and remarks that this is going beautifully, no dictionary entry has been violated. Every word retains its ordinary sense, and the intended meaning nevertheless sits at some distance from the sum of those senses. Any adequate account must therefore explain how a hearer selects a reading that the words do not encode.

Response-time studies indicate that ironic interpretation is not uniformly slower than literal interpretation, contrary to earlier expectations. Delays appear when the context is thin and vanish when the situation strongly supports the ironic reading, which suggests that hearers are not first computing a literal meaning and then discarding it. Instead they appear to weigh several candidate readings against expectation. The relevant expectation concerns what a reasonable speaker would plausibly be doing here, and mismatch with that expectation functions as the trigger.

Prosody supplies powerful cues in speech, though the cues are less standardized than folk accounts assume. A flattened contour, a lengthened vowel and a slight pause before the evaluative word all raise the probability of an ironic reading, yet none is necessary and none is sufficient. Written contexts lack these signals altogether, which is why irony in text depends disproportionately on shared background and why it fails so spectacularly across audiences that do not share it. The failure is informative rather than accidental, since it exposes how much of the work was being done by assumed common ground.

Developmental findings suggest a long acquisition curve, extending far past the mastery of metaphor. Children of eight typically detect that a speaker is being unkind before they can articulate that the speaker means the opposite of the utterance. The ability to detect gentle self-directed irony emerges later still. Adults vary considerably as well, and the variation correlates less with vocabulary size than with familiarity with the speaker. That places a social relationship rather than a lexicon at the centre of the phenomenon.

One methodological caution deserves emphasis. Almost all experimental materials are constructed by researchers who already know which reading is intended, and constructed irony tends to be tidier than the spontaneous variety. Recordings from unscripted conversation contain a substantial proportion of cases in which participants themselves later disagreed about whether the remark had been ironic. If competent native speakers cannot always adjudicate, then irony may be better modelled as a negotiated outcome than as a message successfully decoded.
qs: Read as a whole, what conclusion does this article reach about hearing irony?
Irony is carried by prosody rather than by any shared background.
Irony is worked out between speakers rather than sent as a fixed message.
Irony is triggered by mismatch with expectation rather than by word meaning.
Irony is acquired late rather than early, and the research has tidied the curve.

qs.evidence: If competent native speakers cannot always adjudicate, then irony may be better modelled as a negotiated outcome than as a message successfully decoded.
qs.answer: Irony is worked out between speakers rather than sent as a fixed message.
qs.why: Kalimat penutupnya memilih satu model atas model lain: hasil yang dirundingkan, bukan pesan yang berhasil didekode, karena penutur jati sendiri kadang nggak sepakat.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi memakai rangka “X rather than Y” yang sama, jadi tanda itu nggak lagi menunjuk jawaban. Opsi prosodi bertabrakan dengan “none is necessary and none is sufficient” dan dengan paragraf tiga, yang menyandarkan ironi tertulis pada latar bersama. Opsi pemicu ketidaksesuaian adalah mekanisme paragraf dua, satu langkah di dalam argumennya. Opsi penguasaan yang lambat menggabungkan paragraf empat dan catatan metode paragraf lima, sedangkan kesimpulannya dinyatakan “better modelled as a negotiated outcome”.

qs: What do the response-time findings suggest about how hearers process irony?
Hearers weigh candidate readings at once instead of working in stages.
Hearers compute the literal sense first and then set it quietly aside.
Hearers need thin contexts before any literal reading gets computed at all.
Hearers stop checking the words once the situation makes the joke obvious.

qs.evidence: Delays appear when the context is thin and vanish when the situation strongly supports the ironic reading, which suggests that hearers are not first computing a literal meaning and then discarding it.
qs.answer: Hearers weigh candidate readings at once instead of working in stages.
qs.why: Klausa penutup kalimat itu menolak model bertahap secara terbuka, dan kalimat sesudahnya menyebut pendengar menimbang beberapa bacaan sekaligus terhadap harapan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Ketiga pengecoh menyebut mekanisme sejelas kunci. Opsi makna harfiah lebih dulu dan opsi konteks tipis sebagai syarat sama-sama ditolak klausa “hearers are not first computing a literal meaning and then discarding it”. Opsi berhenti memeriksa kata menambahkan mekanisme yang nggak disebut, sebab teks justru menyebut beberapa bacaan ditimbang sekaligus terhadap harapan.

qs: What is the writer's attitude towards the standard experimental materials?
Confident, treating the tidiness of the materials as a strength of the design.
Dismissive, treating materials of that kind as evidence of very little.
Cautious, treating the materials as tidier than the speech they stand for.
Grateful, treating the unscripted recordings as a defence of the standard method.

qs.evidence: Almost all experimental materials are constructed by researchers who already know which reading is intended, and constructed irony tends to be tidier than the spontaneous variety.
qs.answer: Cautious, treating the materials as tidier than the speech they stand for.
qs.why: Paragraf itu dibuka “One methodological caution deserves emphasis”, dan kalimat ini menyebut ironi buatan lebih rapi daripada ironi spontan; peringatan, bukan penolakan.
qs.whyOthersFail: Keempat opsi memakai rangka “Sifat, treating X as Y” yang sama. Opsi yakin bertabrakan dengan “One methodological caution deserves emphasis”. Opsi meremehkan melampaui teks, yang tetap memakai temuan eksperimen itu di paragraf dua. Opsi bersyukur membalik fungsi rekaman tak berskrip, yang dipakai untuk menunjukkan kelemahan bahan buatan.
